advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, outer_wall_s=1500, seed=42, rationale=iter-1 feasibility, per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394) on breast_ct (Sidky synthetic breast, 128-view sparse, real-mu range, 512^2) - BILATERAL variant. Short warm-start pre-pass (3 ep x 200 train, GT-free N2I self-sup loss) captures a generic BF-sigma init, then per-scene Adam (n_iter=300) on EACH of 16 val scans' own measurements, scored by evaluate_calibrated on the SAME val scenes as every other breast_ct method. Bilateral stack = 6 trainable params (proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1, 3 sigma each); ~2x faster than the U-Net N2I. lr=5e-3 per Wagner-2022 BF recipe (solver CONFIG default); BF sigmas left at Wagner abdomen defaults for the iter-1 feasibility seed (the breast-tuned proj_sx=0.01/proj_sy=0.3/proj_sr=0.0005 from solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md hints is reserved as a clean iter-2 one-knob change). grad_clip=1.0 cheap insurance (breast 128-view adjoint is mild vs Mayo 2304-view). Sizing vs smoke: Mayo 2304-view BILATERAL smoke (job 764666) ran 6*... at ~0.125 s/(iter x scene); breast_ct is 128-view (18x fewer angles) so per-step is much cheaper. Steps = warm <=3x200=600 + per-image 16x300=4800 -> conservatively <700 s at Mayo's bilateral rate, far less on breast's lighter adjoint, well under the claude_agentic_one_iter.sbatch 00:30:00 (1800 s) wall. outer_wall_s=1500 is a hard internal guard on the per-image loop. Hypothesis: per-image bilateral N2I trains stably on breast_ct (finite val_score, comparison.png) and gives a usable per-scene recon; expect hr near the FBP baseline since N2I is structurally bounded by FBP on this dense-view substrate (the prior AMORTISED bilateral N2I was hr=0 / over-smoothing per solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md - the per-image rewrite is what is being tested here).

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005, outer_wall_s=1500, seed=42, rationale=iter-2, ONE-KNOB change vs iter-1: projection-domain BF sigmas swapped from Wagner-abdomen defaults (proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02) to the breast-tuned (proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005). EVERYTHING else identical to iter-1 (warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, grad_clip=1.0, lr=5e-3, proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1, 6 trainable BF params, seed=42). FAILURE MODE addressed: iter-1 hr=0 (val_score 0.9720, PSNR 38.17 vs LD-FBP baseline 39.68 - UNDER baseline). solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md Weaknesses + Hints: the Wagner-abdomen proj sigmas (proj_sx=1.0 -> radial blur after FBP; proj_sy=2.0 -> angular over-smoothing) are TOO AGGRESSIVE for 128-view sparse breast-CT - they radially blur the sparse-view reconstruction on top of the existing streaks, smearing fibroglandular detail. The breast-tuned values (proven sensible from breast-ct-claude-agentic-dual-domain-bf-search-20260521-01) shrink proj_sx to near-identity (0.01, avoids radial blur), keep modest angular interpolation (proj_sy=0.3, mild help for sparse views), and tighten the range sigma (proj_sr=0.0005 << data range, preserves the breast/air attenuation edge in the sinogram). HYPOTHESIS: with the proj-domain BF near-identity + edge-preserving instead of radially blurring, per-image bilateral N2I stops smearing the FBP and recovers PSNR toward (ideally above) the 39.68 LD-FBP baseline, lifting hr off 0. WALL: identical step budget to iter-1 (warm <=3x200=600 + per-image 16x300=4800), which completed in 241 s - far under the 1800 s sbatch wall; outer_wall_s=1500 internal guard unchanged.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0005, outer_wall_s=1500, seed=42, rationale=iter-3, ONE-KNOB change vs iter-1 (the BEST base: PSNR 38.17 dB, SSIM 0.9720). Knob: image-domain BF range sigma img_sr 0.02 -> 0.0005. EVERYTHING else identical to iter-1 (warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, grad_clip=1.0, lr=5e-3, proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1, 6 trainable BF params, seed=42, proj sigmas back at Wagner-abdomen solver defaults). NUMBERS / WHY NOT iter-2's base: iter-2 tuned the PROJECTION-domain sigmas (proj_sx=0.01/proj_sy=0.3/proj_sr=0.0005) and PSNR went DOWN 38.17->37.90 dB (SSIM 0.9720->0.9680, RMSE up). So the proj-domain BF is NOT the over-smoother to fix here; reverting proj sigmas to iter-1 defaults and keeping iter-1 as the base. FAILURE MODE: hr=0, recon below the 39.68 dB LD-FBP baseline because the 6-param BF degrades an already-decent 128-view FBP. The design doc (solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md Weaknesses) pinpoints the IMAGE-domain BF as the over-smoother on breast-CT: 'Image-domain sigma_x grew 0.5->1.08 in 2 epochs on breast-CT iter-1 - saturating the kernel'; and the doc's own rule 'sigma_r << data range preserves edges; sigma_r >> data range degenerates to a Gaussian'. The CONFIG default img_sr=0.02 is too loose for the breast mu-range, so the image-domain BF degenerates toward a plain Gaussian that smooths ACROSS fibroglandular edges. HYPOTHESIS: tightening img_sr to 0.0005 (<< breast attenuation range) makes the image-domain BF edge-preserving instead of a Gaussian blur, so it stops smearing fibroglandular detail in the FBP and recovers PSNR toward (ideally above) the 39.68 dB LD-FBP baseline, lifting hr off 0. This mirrors the tight range-sigma logic the doc recommends for proj_sr, applied to the image domain where the over-smoothing actually lives. WALL: identical step budget to iter-1/2 (warm <=3x200=600 + per-image 16x300=4800), which completed in 241 s / 261 s - far under the 1800 s sbatch wall; outer_wall_s=1500 internal guard unchanged.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-1 feasibility, per-image N2I rewrite (commit 1f4c3394) for the BILATERAL dual-domain solver on demo_dl (phantoms, 128-view synthetic, 512^2). Twin of demo_dl_dual_domain_n2i_iter_01 (job 764702): shared training knobs MATCH that combo (train_n=200, val_n=6, n_iter=400, pretrain_epochs=3, outer_wall_s=1200, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42) so both N2I variants are scored by evaluate_calibrated on the SAME 6 val scenes (seed=42 -> identical split). The ONE intended difference is the architecture: BilateralFilterStack denoisers (6 trainable params at proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1) instead of the U-Net. Bilateral knobs seed from the historical demo_dl DD-BF-N2I winner (leaderboard rank-16: proj_k=7, img_k=5, lr=2.3e-3, SSIM 0.7605) plus Wagner-2022 abdomen sigma defaults (proj_sx/sy/sr=1.0/2.0/0.02, img=1.5/1.5/0.02). lr=2.3e-3 (BFs want higher lr than U-Nets; Wagner used 5e-3, historical demo_dl DD-BF used 2.3e-3 -> keep the proven demo_dl value). Sizing: bilateral is ~2x faster per step than the U-Net N2I (Mayo smoke: bilateral ~0.12 s/step vs dual ~0.245 s/step at 2304 views; demo_dl is 128-view = 18x fewer angles so per-step is far cheaper). Steps = warm 3x200=600 + per-image 6x400=2400 = 3000 total; even at the conservative U-Net rate this is ~360-735 s wall, well under the generic claude_agentic_one_iter.sbatch 00:30:00 (1800 s) wall. outer_wall_s=1200 is a hard internal guard on the per-image loop. Hypothesis: per-image N2I trains stably for the BF stack on demo_dl (finite val_score, comparison.png produced) and yields a usable per-scene recon; expect hr near baseline since N2I is structurally bounded by FBP on this dense-/sparse-view phantom substrate and the 6-param BF has minimal capacity (solver_plan.md). This iter-1 establishes the per-image BF baseline; iter-2+ will tune one knob at a time (likely img_n_bf or img kernel/sigma first, per the solver design doc hints).

PIVOT from DEPTH to RANGE-SIGMA TUNING, because depth is now in clear diminishing returns and PSNR has SATURATED. Trajectory: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 val 0.6657/hr+0.2763/PSNR 19.47; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 val 0.7465/hr+0.3276/PSNR 20.10 (+0.081 SSIM, +0.63 dB); iter-3 img_n_bf=5 val 0.7705/hr+0.3335/PSNR 20.18 (+0.024 SSIM, only +0.08 dB). The SSIM deltas are halving each depth step (+0.081 -> +0.024) and PSNR has flatlined (20.10 -> 20.18) -> img_n_bf depth has hit its structural ceiling; one more notch (5->7) would buy <0.012 SSIM at best. The higher-EV move is to make the deep 5-layer cascade we ALREADY have actually edge-preserving. Per docs/runs/mayo_campaign_state.md 'N2I PER-IMAGE knob insights' (confirmed cross-run 2026-06-18/19): on breast/demo (128-view substrates) the IMAGE-domain over-smoothing lever is img_sr, and 'default 0.02 too loose -> degenerates to a Gaussian blur ... Tighten img_sr->0.0005 for edge preservation'. The whole 5-deep cascade currently initialises every layer's RANGE sigma at 0.02, so each of the 5 BFs starts in the loose-Gaussian regime that smooths across phantom edges -> caps SSIM. Tightening img_sr to 0.0005 makes all 5 layers edge-preserving from init (sigma_r << data range preserves edges; sigma_r >> range degenerates to Gaussian, per solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_n2i.md). This maximally leverages the deep cascade (5 layers x tighter range) and targets exactly the SSIM-capping over-smoothing rather than the exhausted PSNR/noise axis. Chose img_sr over img_n_bf 5->7 (exhausted lever, flat PSNR) and over img_kernel (a less-informed guess: kernel sets spatial extent, but the symptom here is range-domain over-smoothing across edges, which img_sr governs directly). Held fixed: img_n_bf=5, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3). Wall: iter-3 ran 235 s; img_sr is an init value, zero added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and 1200 s outer_wall_s guard. Hypothesis: tightening the image-domain range sigma to 0.0005 stops the 5-deep cascade from degenerating into a Gaussian blur across phantom edges, preserving fine structural detail and lifting val_score above iter-3's 0.7705 (the SSIM/edge axis, which still has headroom, not the saturated PSNR/noise axis). If it does NOT move val_score (or regresses), it confirms the image-domain BF range sigma is already effectively tight after training on this substrate and the next iter should pivot to img_kernel (spatial extent) or img spatial sigmas.

Trajectory: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 val 0.6657/hr+0.2763/PSNR 19.47; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 val 0.7465/hr+0.3276/PSNR 20.10; iter-3 img_n_bf=5 val 0.7705/hr+0.3335/PSNR 20.18 (HR-BEST); iter-4 tightened img_sr 0.02->0.0005 -> SSIM ticked up to 0.7709 but hr COLLAPSED 0.3335->0.1998 and PSNR fell 20.18->18.60. Failure mode: tight img_sr is the WRONG lever for demo's substrate. The mayo_campaign_state.md 'tighten img_sr->0.0005 for edge preservation' insight is BREAST-specific (tight=good on dense fibroglandular breast); on demo's sparse ellipse phantoms the tight range sigma OVER-SHARPENS - it forces the 5-deep image cascade to act only across hard intensity jumps and stop smoothing the broad noise floor, so noise/PSNR worsens (20.18->18.60 dB) even though the SSIM structural term inches up. headroom is the campaign's primary structurally-bounded score and it is PSNR/noise-sensitive here, so the over-sharpen is net-negative. The img_sr lever is SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC and OPPOSITE between breast (tight=good) and demo (loose=good). Reverting img_sr 0.0005->0.02 restores the iter-3 hr-0.3335 regime, where the loose range sigma lets the deep cascade do its proven coarse-to-fine NOISE smoothing (the demo lever that earned hr 0.276->0.328->0.335 via img_n_bf 1->3->5 at img_sr=0.02). Chose the clean SINGLE-numeric-knob revert (img_sr only) over also pushing img_n_bf 5->7 in the same iter, to first cleanly RECOVER hr 0.3335 and re-confirm the loose-img_sr regime before iter-6 pushes the proven depth lever further. Held fixed at the iter-3/iter-4 values: img_n_bf=5, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3/4). Wall: iter-4 ran 264 s; img_sr is an init value, zero added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s guard. Hypothesis: reverting the image-domain range sigma to the looser 0.02 undoes the iter-4 over-sharpen and recovers val_score/hr to ~iter-3 (SSIM ~0.7705, hr ~0.3335, PSNR ~20.18), confirming that on demo's substrate loose img_sr is correct (opposite to breast). If hr does NOT recover to ~0.3335, it would mean the iter-4 regression was NOT purely the img_sr lever (re-examine seed/split determinism) - but per the identical-split protocol it should land back on iter-3.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-6: ONE knob changed vs the hr-best base iter-3/iter-5 (img_n_bf 5->7, the image-domain bilateral cascade DEPTH); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_05.json (which restored iter-3, img_n_bf=5/img_sr=0.02, hr 0.3320~0.3335 = run-best). Base chosen by HEADROOM, not raw SSIM: hr is the campaign primary metric and is PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo. Trajectory by HEADROOM: iter-1 img_n_bf=1 hr 0.2763 (PSNR 19.47); iter-2 img_n_bf=3 hr 0.3276 (PSNR 20.10, +0.051); iter-3 img_n_bf=5 hr 0.3335 (PSNR 20.18, +0.007 HR-BEST); iter-4 img_sr->0.0005 hr 0.1998 REGRESSED (wrong-direction range-sigma lever, over-sharpen, PSNR 18.60); iter-5 img_sr->0.02 revert hr 0.3320 RECOVERED to ~iter-3. The img_sr range-sigma lever is EXHAUSTED and substrate-confirmed: demo wants LOOSE img_sr=0.02 (opposite to breast), tightening HURTS hr. The proj-domain stack is in the symmetry trap (proj sigmas near-identity per the design doc -> proj_n_bf stays 1, wasted params). That leaves image-domain DEPTH (img_n_bf) as the only proven hr lever on demo, the same lever that earned the whole arc hr 0.276->0.328->0.335. PROBE/HYPOTHESIS: push the proven depth lever one notch further, 5->7, growing the image denoiser from 15 to 21 trainable scalars (total network 16->22 params, still ultra-low, far too few to memorise 6 val scenes). Two more BFs add two coarse-to-fine scales to the multi-scale cascade for additional noise-floor smoothing -- the demo-relevant axis since hr here is PSNR/noise-sensitive. This DOUBLES as the ceiling-doc probe: depth gains are sharply diminishing (1->3 gave +0.051 hr, 3->5 gave only +0.007 hr, PSNR flat 20.10->20.18), so expect <=+0.003 hr. If hr flattens (or regresses), it CONFIRMS demo bilateral N2I is at its structural ceiling (~hr 0.33) -- the 21-scalar image cascade cannot extract more than the half-view FBP noise floor allows on this 128-view synthetic phantom substrate -- and the next iter should stop chasing depth and instead document the ceiling (seed/n_iter/pretrain_epochs invariance probe) rather than tune another smoothing knob. Chose img_n_bf 5->7 over (a) img_sr (exhausted, wrong-direction, hr 0.3335->0.1998), (b) proj_n_bf (symmetry trap, wasted params), (c) img_kernel/img_sx/img_sy (less-informed guesses with no headroom evidence) -- depth is the ONLY lever with a demonstrated positive hr slope on demo. Held fixed at iter-3/iter-5 values: img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1/2/3/4/5). Wall: iter-5 ran 249 s; two more image-domain BFs add only a small fraction of the 128-view FBP+proj per-step cost, so comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (well under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=800, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-7: ONE knob changed vs iter-6 (n_iter 400->800, the per-scan Adam fit budget); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_06.json (img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct). CEILING-DOC PROBE, not another smoothing knob. Trajectory by HEADROOM (the campaign primary metric, PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo): iter-1 img_n_bf=1 hr 0.2763 (PSNR 19.47); iter-2 n_bf=3 hr 0.3276 (+0.051); iter-3 n_bf=5 hr 0.3335 (+0.006, depth HR-BEST); iter-4 img_sr->0.0005 hr 0.1998 REGRESSED; iter-5 img_sr->0.02 revert hr 0.3320 recovered; iter-6 n_bf=7 hr 0.3330 (+0.000 vs n_bf=5, SSIM +0.009 0.7705->0.7796 but hr DEAD FLAT). FAILURE MODE: the image-domain DEPTH lever (img_n_bf) has hit its HEADROOM ceiling -- depth still lifts the SSIM structural term but its hr slope collapsed to zero by n_bf=5 (slope +0.051 -> +0.006 -> 0.000). img_sr is exhausted and substrate-confirmed wrong-direction (demo wants LOOSE 0.02; tightening collapses hr). proj_n_bf is in the symmetry trap (near-identity proj sigmas -> wasted params). So all the SMOOTHING/CAPACITY axes are exhausted on hr. The remaining open question for the ceiling claim is OPTIMIZATION budget: is hr ~0.333 the half-view FBP noise-floor bound (structural), or is the per-scan Adam fit simply stopping short at n_iter=400? Per the per-image N2I knob insights (mayo_campaign_state.md): U-Net N2I OVERFITS each scan as n_iter rises (no early-stop -> demo-n2i 0.4785->0.4293 @n_iter1200), but the 6-param BILATERAL physically CANNOT overfit one scan -- so doubling its per-scan budget is the clean diagnostic the U-Net could not give: more steps either (a) lift hr -> the plateau was under-optimization, the lever is n_iter (and lr), not depth; or (b) leave hr flat at ~0.333 -> CONFIRMS the structural half-view FBP ceiling, after which iter-8+ should stop tuning and document the ceiling with a seed/pretrain_epochs invariance probe toward iter-20. Chose n_iter over (a) img_n_bf 7->9 (depth lever's hr slope is already zero -- a 4th depth step re-confirms iter-6 with near-zero EV on hr), (b) lr (would confound the budget question -- vary n_iter first at the proven lr=2.3e-3, then lr if n_iter moves hr), (c) img_kernel/img_sx/img_sy (less-informed smoothing guesses, no hr evidence). Held fixed at iter-6 values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1..6). Wall: iter-6 ran ~260 s; doubling the per-scan fit roughly doubles the per-image loop to ~450-520 s, still well under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). Hypothesis: hr stays ~0.333 even at n_iter=800 -- the 6-param bilateral cannot overfit and has already converged on the half-view FBP noise floor, so more fit budget yields no hr -> CONFIRMS demo bilateral N2I is at its structural ~hr 0.33 ceiling toward iter-20. If instead hr rises meaningfully (>+0.005), the plateau was optimizer-budget-limited and n_iter (then lr) becomes the live lever. PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.

FAILURE MODE: the image-domain DEPTH lever (img_n_bf) has hit its HEADROOM ceiling -- depth still lifts the SSIM structural term but its hr slope collapsed to zero by n_bf=5 (slope +0.051 -> +0.006 -> 0.000). img_sr is exhausted and substrate-confirmed wrong-direction (demo wants LOOSE 0.02; tightening collapses hr). proj_n_bf is in the symmetry trap (near-identity proj sigmas -> wasted params). Held fixed at iter-6 values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 (-> identical val split, directly comparable to iter-1..6). Wall: iter-6 ran ~260 s; doubling the per-scan fit roughly doubles the per-image loop to ~450-520 s, still well under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). Hypothesis: hr stays ~0.333 even at n_iter=800 -- the 6-param bilateral cannot overfit and has already converged on the half-view FBP noise floor, so more fit budget yields no hr -> CONFIRMS demo bilateral N2I is at its structural ~hr 0.33 ceiling toward iter-20. If instead hr rises meaningfully (>+0.005), the plateau was optimizer-budget-limited and n_iter (then lr) becomes the live lever. PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.

Read iters 6->8 BY HEADROOM (campaign primary, PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo): iter-6 img_n_bf=7 seed=42 hr 0.3330 (PSNR 20.18); iter-7 n_iter 400->800 seed=42 hr 0.3346 (PSNR 20.19, per-scan Adam budget DEAD FLAT); iter-8 seed 42->123 hr 0.4222 BUT PSNR DROPPED to 17.81 and SSIM dipped 0.7796->0.7711. FAILURE MODE at hr~0.42: the headroom estimate is HIGH-VARIANCE across the tiny val_n=6 draw. A pure seed change (iter-8) swung hr +0.089 (0.333->0.422) while PSNR fell -2.4 dB and SSIM fell -0.0085 -- hr and PSNR moved in OPPOSITE directions, which a genuine reconstruction improvement cannot do. The hr jump is therefore an EASIER 6-scene val draw (weaker LD-FBP baseline inflating the headroom fraction (metric-baseline)/(oracle-baseline)), NOT a real lift. iter-8 pre-registered exactly this next step: If hr instead swings widely, the ceiling is split-sensitive and val_n should be raised next to tighten the estimate. HYPOTHESIS (the variance hypothesis): doubling val_n 6->12 tightens the hr estimate; if hr 0.4222 was a lucky-split artifact it regresses toward the ~0.36-0.39 midpoint of the two single-split readings (0.333 & 0.422), and PSNR recovers toward ~19 dB as the larger draw re-includes harder scenes. If instead hr stays ~0.42 at val_n=12, the lift is real and seed-123s draw was representative -- either way the campaigns reported demo-bilateral number is de-noised. Chose val_n over (a) img_n_bf/n_iter (both DEAD FLAT, exhausted at seed=42), (b) img_sr (exhausted + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction: tightening to 0.0005 collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- do NOT repeat), (c) proj_n_bf (symmetry trap, wasted params), (d) lr/grad_clip/warm_start/pretrain_epochs (untried but not yet motivated -- the iter-8 PSNR-vs-hr divergence makes VARIANCE the named open question, and val_n is its direct test). Held fixed at iter-8 PEAK values: seed=123, img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), n_iter=400, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, grad_clip=1.0. Wall: iter-8 ran 345 s at val_n=6/n_iter=400; doubling val_n roughly doubles the per-scene fit portion -> est ~600-700 s, well under the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard and the 1800 s sbatch wall (under the 15-min budget). This iter DOCUMENTS whether the hr~0.42 champion is a real lift or a val-split artifact, toward iter-20. PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.05, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-11: ONE knob changed vs the iter-6 hr-0.4222 PEAK base (proj_sr 0.02->0.05, the PROJECTION-domain bilateral RANGE sigma); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_06.json (img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct, proj_n_bf=1, proj_k=7/img_k=5, proj_sx/sy=1.0/2.0, img_sx/sy=1.5/1.5, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42 -> identical seed=42 val split, directly comparable to iter-6 hr 0.3330 / PSNR 20.18 / SSIM 0.7796). PROBE A PROJECTION-DOMAIN KNOB IN THE LOOSE DIRECTION -- the only proven-safe direction on demo and the one axis never touched at the PEAK. Read iters 9->10 BY HEADROOM (campaign primary, PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo): iter-9 val_n 6->12 at seed=123 CONFIRMED hr~0.41 is REAL (0.4099, PSNR 18.61) -- not a lucky 6-scene draw; iter-10 pretrain_epochs 3->6 DEAD FLAT (hr 0.3328, PSNR ~iter-6) -> the warm-start amortized anchor is already SATURATED at 3 epochs. FAILURE MODE at hr~0.42: the 6-param bilateral sits at its structural noise-floor ceiling on the 64-view (half of 128) FBP, and EVERY image-side + anchor lever is now EXHAUSTED: image-domain DEPTH (img_n_bf, hr slope collapsed to ~0 by n_bf=5: 1->3 +0.051, 3->5 +0.006, 5->7 +0.000), per-scan OPTIMIZER budget (n_iter flat 400->800; the 6-param BF physically CANNOT overfit one scan), warm-start anchor length (pretrain_epochs flat 3->6). img_sr is EXHAUSTED + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction (demo wants LOOSE 0.02; tightening to 0.0005 collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- do NOT repeat). What has NEVER been perturbed at the PEAK is the PROJECTION-domain stack. The standing claim (design doc + mayo_campaign_state.md) is that the proj stack is in a 'symmetry trap' -> proj_n_bf stays 1, wasted params. BUT that claim was only ever tested via proj_n_bf DEPTH (stacking more near-identity filters) -- the proj RANGE sigma itself was pinned at proj_sr=0.02 the entire run. A single near-identity proj BF at proj_sr=0.02 behaves almost as a pass-through in the sinogram domain (range kernel too tight to act on the noisy 64-view sinogram), which is PRECISELY why stacking it (proj_n_bf>1) is wasted. HYPOTHESIS (proj-range): LOOSENING proj_sr 0.02->0.05 widens the single proj BF range kernel so it actually smooths sinogram-domain noise BEFORE the FBP adjoint (a denoising axis ORTHOGONAL to the exhausted image-domain levers), giving the dual-domain pipeline genuine projection-domain denoising it has lacked -> lifts hr/PSNR above the iter-6 ~0.333 / PSNR 20.18 baseline on the SAME seed=42 split. Direction is LOOSE (demo confirmed-correct direction; mirrors the image-domain finding that demo wants LOOSE range sigma) -- the OPPOSITE of the forbidden img_sr tightening. If hr/PSNR stay FLAT, it CONFIRMS the proj stack is genuinely structurally inert on this 128-view phantom substrate even with a loosened range kernel (the symmetry-trap claim holds for the RANGE axis too, not just depth) and the ~hr 0.33 ceiling is image-domain-FBP-bounded -- a clean ceiling-doc result toward iter-20. Chose proj_sr (LOOSE) over (a) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs (all DEAD FLAT, exhausted), (b) img_sr (exhausted + WRONG-direction -- forbidden), (c) proj_n_bf depth (symmetry trap -- stacking a near-identity filter is the wasted-param move; loosening the SINGLE filter range is the un-tested alternative), (d) grad_clip (mandatory overflow guard at 1.0, not a quality lever). Held fixed at iter-6 PEAK values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. Wall: iter-6 ran 828 s; proj_sr is a pure init value with ZERO added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (under the 15-min budget). PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized.

PUSH THE SAME WINNING LEVER FURTHER. Read iter-13 BY SSIM/HEADROOM (campaign primary; SSIM is the surface the spatial lever moved): iter-13 widened img_sx/img_sy 1.5->2.5 and LIFTED SSIM 0.7796->0.7940 (+0.0144, the run best), while hr stayed FLAT at 0.3332 (~iter-6 0.3330) -- the image-domain SPATIAL sigma is the FIRST lever in the whole run to break the SSIM plateau (img_n_bf depth had saturated SSIM growth and hr; proj domain fully inert at iter-11/12). FAILURE MODE iter-13 addressed and this iter re-probes: the 7-deep image bilateral cascade was UNDER-SMOOTHING the broad post-FBP noise floor at the default spatial sigma 1.5 -- widening the spatial neighborhood (sigma 1.5->2.5) let each of the 7 image BFs average over a larger support and smooth that broad noise floor, lifting the structural-similarity term while the LOOSE img_sr=0.02 kept it edge-preserving (no blur across phantom edges). The open question: does the image-domain spatial sigma KEEP lifting SSIM past 0.7940 as it widens further (3.5), or does it SATURATE / regress? HYPOTHESIS (img-spatial-2): widening img_sx/img_sy 2.5->3.5 enlarges the averaging support further, smoothing the residual noise floor more -> may lift SSIM above iter-13 0.7940 on the SAME seed=42 split (note whether hr moves too -- iter-13 SSIM rose but hr stayed 0.333, so the spatial lever may be an SSIM-only axis bounded by the same 64-view-FBP hr ceiling). KEY DIAGNOSTIC / RISK: img_kernel is held at 5, so the discrete bilateral WINDOW is +/-2 px. At sigma 2.5 the Gaussian spatial weight is already near-flat across that 5-px window (iter-13 noted 2.5 is near the window edge); at sigma 3.5 the spatial weight is even FLATTER -> the kernel=5 window, not the sigma, may now be the binding constraint, in which case SSIM saturates (or moves only marginally) because the BF can't actually reach the wider support the sigma requests. If SSIM SATURATES or regresses here, that pinpoints img_kernel (window SIZE) as the iter-15 lever -- widen img_kernel 5->7/9 to let the larger spatial sigma act over a genuinely larger window (the pre-registered next step from iter-13's rationale: 'img_kernel is the iter-14 candidate if img_sx/sy moves hr' -- img_sx/sy DID move SSIM, so kernel is now the live follow-on once sigma saturates). If SSIM KEEPS rising, the spatial sigma still has headroom inside the kernel=5 window and iter-15 pushes sigma further (4.5) before touching the kernel. Chose img_sx/img_sy 2.5->3.5 (the SAME winning lever, one notch further -- the steer's explicit instruction) over (a) img_kernel (the natural follow-on, but only AFTER confirming whether sigma alone saturates inside the current window -- changing kernel now would confound the sigma-saturation question), (b) proj_sr/proj_kernel/proj_n_bf (whole proj domain confirmed flat at iter-11/12 -- symmetry trap, wasted), (c) img_sr (exhausted + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction -- tightening collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- FORBIDDEN, do NOT tighten; stays LOOSE 0.02), (d) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs/seed/val_n (all DEAD FLAT / variance-only, exhausted), (e) grad_clip (mandatory overflow guard at 1.0, not a quality lever). Read iter-16->17 BY SSIM (the surface the spatial-smoothing thread moves; hr stays pinned ~0.325-0.332 at the 64-view-FBP noise-floor ceiling, an SSIM-only lever): iter-16 img_kernel 7->9 gave SSIM 0.8246->0.8284 (+0.0038, kernel thread saturating at the then-sigma=3.5); iter-17 RE-LIBERATED the sigma img_sx/img_sy 3.5->4.5 at kernel=9 and LIFTED SSIM 0.8284->0.8368 (+0.0084, STILL CLIMBING -- bigger than the saturating iter-16 kernel step), while hr stayed pinned (0.3283->0.3251) and PSNR flat (20.12->20.08). So sigma re-liberation is the live thread and it is NOT yet saturated. SIGMA/KERNEL COUPLING READ (the binding constraint flipped back to the WINDOW): a Gaussian of spatial sigma s needs ~+/-2s of support to be well-represented; at img_sx=4.5 that is ~+/-9px requested, but img_kernel=9 gives only a +/-4px window (half-window 4 < sigma 4.5). So the sigma=4.5 Gaussian is AGAIN truncated by the window -- the +0.0084 lift at iter-17 was the sigma reaching the +/-4px window edge, and the WINDOW is once more the binding constraint (2*sigma~9px > 4px half-window). FAILURE MODE this iter addresses: at kernel=9 the img_sx=4.5 spatial weight is clipped at the +/-4px window edge -- the BF cannot average over the full ~+/-5px (kernel=11) / ~+/-9px (2*sigma) neighborhood the sigma=4.5 requests. The unlock is to widen the WINDOW, not push the sigma further (pushing sigma 4.5->5.5 now would request even MORE support from a window that already truncates it -- the exact iter-14 saturation regime). This is the alternating sigma<->kernel ladder explicitly pre-registered in iter-17's rationale: 'If SSIM rises meaningfully, the sigma still has headroom and the alternating sigma<->kernel ladder continues (iter-18 would widen kernel 9->11)'. SSIM rose +0.0084 (meaningfully), so the ladder continues to the kernel. HYPOTHESIS (img-kernel-3): widening img_kernel 9->11 enlarges each per-BF window from +/-4px to +/-5px so the img_sx=4.5 spatial Gaussian can average over (more of) the neighborhood it requests -> lifts SSIM past iter-17 0.8368 on the SAME seed=42 split. Expect hr to stay pinned ~0.325-0.332 (this whole spatial thread is an SSIM-only structural-similarity lever bounded by the 64-view-FBP noise floor -- hr flat across iter-13..17). DIAGNOSTIC: if SSIM rises meaningfully (gain >0.005) the climb continues and iter-19 would RE-LIBERATE the sigma again (4.5->5.5 now that kernel=11 admits it) -- the ladder is not yet at its substrate bound; if SSIM SATURATES or regresses (gain <0.005) the image-domain spatial denoising is exhausted at the ~0.84 SSIM / ~0.33 hr substrate bound -- the 6-param bilateral cannot extract more than the 64-view (half of 128) FBP noise floor allows on this synthetic phantom substrate -- a clean ceiling-doc result toward iter-20. Held fixed at iter-17 values: img_sx=4.5/img_sy=4.5, img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sr=0.02, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; warm_start STAYS ON; do NOT revert to amortized; do NOT tighten img_sr.

DECISIVE SATURATION TEST of the alternating sigma<->kernel ladder. Read iter-17->18 BY SSIM (the surface the spatial-smoothing thread moves; hr stays pinned ~0.325-0.333 at the 64-view-FBP noise-floor ceiling, an SSIM-only lever): iter-17 RE-LIBERATED sigma img_sx/img_sy 3.5->4.5 at kernel=9 -> SSIM 0.8284->0.8368 (+0.0084, ABOVE the 0.005 'meaningful' threshold); iter-18 widened kernel 9->11 -> SSIM 0.8368->0.8401 (+0.0033, BELOW the 0.005 threshold), hr flat 0.3251->0.3256, PSNR flat 20.08->20.09. The whole ladder trajectory: img_n_bf depth saturated SSIM/hr early; the image SPATIAL thread then climbed via alternating sigma<->kernel rungs -- SSIM 0.7796(iter6) ->0.7940(s2.5) ->0.8035(s3.5) ->0.8246(k7) ->0.8284(k9) ->0.8368(s4.5) ->0.8401(k11). The rung gains are decelerating: the sigma rungs gave +0.0144, +0.0095, +0.0084; the kernel rungs gave +0.0211, +0.0038, +0.0033. The LAST kernel rung (iter-18, +0.0033) fell BELOW the agent's own 0.005 meaningful-gain threshold -- the WINDOW lever is now exhausted. FAILURE-MODE / COUPLING DIAGNOSIS being tested: under the pre-registered ladder logic the next rung is the SIGMA (kernel just gave a sub-threshold step), but the coupling math warns this rung is near or past its substrate bound. A Gaussian of spatial sigma s needs ~+/-2s of support to be well-represented; at kernel=11 the window is +/-5px, while sigma=5.5 requests ~+/-11px (2*sigma) -- so sigma=5.5 is AGAIN window-truncated (half-window 5 < sigma 5.5), the same over-request regime that flattened iter-14. So this rung tests EXACTLY whether ANY residual sigma headroom remains inside the kernel=11 window: at kernel=9 the sigma re-lib 3.5->4.5 still paid +0.0084 because the window (then +/-4) had just been widened ahead of the sigma; here the window is only +/-5px for a requested +/-11px Gaussian, so the marginal extra averaging the window can actually deliver is small. HYPOTHESIS (img-spatial-4, ceiling-doc): widening img_sx/img_sy 4.5->5.5 at kernel=11 yields a SUB-THRESHOLD SSIM gain (<0.005) or regresses, while hr stays pinned ~0.325-0.333 and PSNR flat ~20.1 -- CONFIRMING the image-domain spatial-denoising ladder has reached the ~0.84 SSIM / ~0.33 hr substrate bound: the 6-param bilateral cannot extract more than the 64-view (half of 128) FBP noise floor allows on this synthetic phantom substrate. If instead SSIM rises meaningfully (>0.005), the sigma still has headroom even inside the +/-5px window and iter-20 would widen the kernel one final notch (11->13) to confirm the ladder is genuinely climbing rather than at its bound -- either way iter-19 cleanly resolves box-(4): does the climb continue past 0.8401 or has image-domain spatial denoising hit the ~0.84 SSIM substrate bound? Chose img_sx/img_sy 4.5->5.5 (the pre-registered ladder continuation -- the SIGMA rung, since the kernel just delivered a sub-threshold +0.0033) over (a) pushing img_kernel 11->13 NOW (the kernel rung just fell below the 0.005 threshold at iter-18 -- the window is no longer the binding lever, and widening it further with the unchanged sigma=4.5 it already mostly contains is the lowest-EV move), (b) proj_sr/proj_kernel/proj_n_bf (whole proj domain confirmed flat at iter-11/12 -- symmetry trap, wasted), (c) img_sr (exhausted + substrate-confirmed WRONG-direction -- tightening to 0.0005 collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4 -- FORBIDDEN, stays LOOSE 0.02), (d) img_n_bf/n_iter/pretrain_epochs/seed/val_n (all DEAD FLAT / variance-only, exhausted), (e) grad_clip (mandatory overflow guard at 1.0, not a quality lever). Held fixed at iter-18 values: img_kernel=11, img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), proj_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=7, proj_sr=0.02, proj_sx=1.0/proj_sy=2.0, lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42. DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-1 lr1e-3/n_iter400 SSIM 0.4785; iter-2 n_iter1200 0.4293 (more per-scan steps HURT -> per-image overfit, n_iter ruled out); iter-3 lr1e-3->1e-4 0.4880 (+0.01, the overfit-anchor lever). The lr-anchor gain was SMALL and exactly as iter-3 predicted: 'at lr=1e-4 the per-image fit barely moves off warm-start' -- so the per-scan recon is now PINNED to the warm-start init. iter-3 named this iter's lever verbatim: 'if SSIM is still flat at ~0.47 the warm-start init itself is the floor and iter-4 should toggle warm_start / raise pretrain_epochs.' SSIM rose only 0.4785->0.4880, i.e. essentially the warm-start floor. FAILURE MODE now = warm-start init is the operating point and is under-trained at 3 epochs; with lr anchored at 1e-4 the per-scan fit cannot escape a poor init, so the init quality is the ceiling. unet_c is NOT the lever (campaign-state: mayo c16->c32 flat 0.9508; solver design doc warns capacity is not the lever for this loss) and n_iter is RULED OUT (iter-2 regressed). HYPOTHESIS: a better-converged warm-start init lifts SSIM above the 0.4880 iter-3 plateau toward the LD-FBP baseline (still structurally FBP-bounded on 128-view, so expect approach-to-baseline / small headroom, not a large jump); if SSIM stays flat at ~0.49 the warm-start pre-pass is already saturated at 3ep and iter-5 should probe warm_start sensitivity (toggle off, or seed). WALL: warm 6x200=1200 + per-image 6x600=3600 = 4800 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 400 s (iter-3 was 340s at 4200 steps), well under the 15-min target, the outer_wall_s=1200 guard, and the 1800 s sbatch wall. KEEP lr=1e-4 (the per-scan overfit anchor, iter-3 winner). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-1 lr1e-3/n_iter400 SSIM 0.4785; iter-2 n_iter1200 0.4293 (more per-scan steps HURT -> per-image U-Net overfits each single noisy scan; n_iter RULED OUT); iter-3 lr1e-3->1e-4 0.4880 (+0.0095, the overfit-anchor lever -> per-scan fit pinned near the warm-start init); iter-4 pretrain_epochs 3->6 0.4957 (+0.0077, the BIGGEST gain, PSNR 16.13->16.29). The two confirmed levers on this dataset are (a) per-scan lr-down anchor and (b) warm-start init quality; n_iter is counterproductive and unet_c is explicitly warned against (solver design doc: capacity is NOT the lever for this loss; mayo n2i sibling c16->c32 flat 0.9508). With lr anchored at 1e-4 the per-scan fit barely moves off the warm-start init, so the warm-start init quality IS the operating point / binding constraint. iter-4 moved init quality MONOTONICALLY up (3ep 0.4880 -> 6ep 0.4957) with NO saturation/turn-over signal -- the lever still has slope. FAILURE MODE = warm-start init still under-converged at 6 epochs; the lr=1e-4 per-scan fit preserves but cannot improve a mediocre init, so a better-converged amortized GT-free N2I pre-pass directly raises the ceiling. LEVER CHOICE: of the two candidates, push pretrain_epochs (the lever that just gave the largest gain and is still climbing) rather than unet_c -- capacity is the warned-against axis and the mayo n2i sibling is already running the c16->c32 capacity probe, so keep the demo probe on the orthogonal init-budget lever instead of duplicating it. HYPOTHESIS: doubling the warm-start budget 6->12 epochs converges the amortized N2I init further, lifting SSIM above the 0.4957 iter-4 plateau toward the LD-FBP baseline (still structurally FBP-bounded on 128-view phantoms, so expect approach-to-baseline / small headroom, not a large jump). FALSIFIER: if SSIM is flat at ~0.495 the warm-start pre-pass has saturated by ~6ep and the init lever is exhausted -> iter-6 should pivot to the per-scan-anchor axis (warm_start sensitivity / seed / lr sweep around 1e-4) or accept the U-Net N2I ceiling and lean on the bilateral twin. WALL: warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 6x600=3600 = 6000 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 500 s (iter-4 was 370s at 4800 steps), well under the 15-min target, the outer_wall_s=1200 guard, and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall. Seed RESET 123 -> 42 (the baseline seed of iters 1-6) so the warm_start ON/OFF contrast is clean against the ep12/seed42 PEAK (0.5081), not confounded by the seed-123 basin. KEEP lr=1e-4 (per-scan overfit anchor, iter-3 winner), pretrain_epochs=12 (the peak init budget -- inert when warm_start=False but left at peak for a clean toggle-back if needed). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): the iter-7 seed probe's FALSIFIER FIRED. Trend ep12/lr1e-4: seed42 SSIM 0.5081 PSNR 16.376 (iter-5 PEAK); seed42/ep18 0.5016 PSNR 16.29 (iter-6); seed123/ep12 0.4203 PSNR 13.085 (iter-7). Flipping ONLY the seed dropped SSIM 0.5081 -> 0.4203 (-0.088) and PSNR 16.38 -> 13.09 dB (-3.3 dB) -- far outside the iter-7 falsifier band (predicted +/-0.01, threshold <0.49). So ~0.51 is NOT a cleanly-converged structural ceiling; the per-image fit has a LARGE stochastic noise floor. FAILURE MODE = the per-scan U-Net N2I operating point is FRAGILE to initialization: the amortized warm-start pre-pass lands in variable basins (seed42 good, seed123 bad), and the lr=1e-4 per-scan fit is anchored to whatever basin it inherits, so init variance -> output variance. n_iter is RULED OUT (iter-2 1200 steps REGRESSED 0.4785->0.4293), pretrain_epochs is EXHAUSTED/turned-over (ep12 peak, ep18 worse), unet_c is the explicitly-warned-against axis, grad_clip=1.0 is LOAD-BEARING (128-view FBP adjoint guard, mandatory -- do NOT touch). LEVER CHOICE (the one untried per-image knob with real headroom): warm_start ON->OFF. This directly tests whether the amortized init is HELPING or is the SOURCE of the seed-fragility: with warm_start=False the per-scan fit starts from a deterministic fresh U-Net (no pre-pass basin lottery), isolating the per-scan N2I objective's own variance. WARM-START-FRAGILITY HYPOTHESIS: the 0.5081->0.4203 seed swing is driven by the warm-start pre-pass landing in variable basins. (a) If warm_start=False SSIM stabilizes near/above ~0.48 with much smaller seed sensitivity, the warm-start was net-fragility (possibly near-neutral on mean) and the per-scan fit alone is the real, more-robust operating point -- a cleaner basis to then re-probe. Either branch is informative toward the iter-20 mandate. hr expected ~0 (structurally FBP-bounded on dense-view phantoms). WALL: warm_start=False ELIMINATES the 12x200=2400-step pre-pass, leaving ONLY per-image 6x600=3600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 300 s (iter-7 was 544 s WITH the pre-pass), comfortably under the 15-min target, the outer_wall_s=1200 guard, and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall -- no need to drop val_n/n_iter. NOT the iter-9 lr2e-4 (dead: 0.4697 confirms 1e-4 optimal), NOT iter-8 warm_start=off (dead: 0.4486), NOT the iter-7 seed123 basin. lr RESET 2e-4 -> 1e-4 (the per-scan overfit-anchor optimum). DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-8 warm_start OFF dropped 0.5081->0.4486 (-0.0595, load-bearing-positive, settled); iter-9 lr 1e-4->2e-4 dropped 0.5081->0.4697 (-0.0384 vs the ep12 peak), so 1e-4 is confirmed the per-scan step optimum at the converged init. BOTH iter-8 and iter-9 came back NEGATIVE, closing warm_start and lr as levers. FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan (the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr0 at ~0.51 SSIM); AND the per-image fit has a LARGE init-driven STOCHASTIC NOISE FLOOR -- a seed flip 42->123 alone swung SSIM 0.5081->0.4203 (-0.088) at the SAME ep12/lr1e-4 config (iter-5 vs iter-7). That noise floor is the real obstacle to *documenting* the ceiling: every single-val read is contaminated by per-scan stochasticity, so 'is 0.51 the converged ceiling or just one lucky/unlucky draw?' is unanswerable at val_n=6. EXHAUSTED axes (do NOT retry): n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps 0.4785->0.4293, U-Net overfits one scan), warm_start (iter-8 off -0.06), lr (iter-3 1e-3->1e-4 + iter-9 1e-4->2e-4 both bracket 1e-4 as optimal), pretrain_epochs (ep12 peak, ep18 worse 0.5016), unet_c (mayo n2i c16->c32 flat 0.9508, design-doc warned-against). grad_clip=1.0 is LOAD-BEARING (the 2304/128-view FBP-adjoint overflow guard, mandatory -- do NOT touch). LEVER CHOICE (the one genuinely-untried knob with real value -- box-3 candidate): val_n 6 -> 12, a CLEANER NOISE-FLOOR READ. Doubling the number of val scenes averages the per-scan SSIM over 2x as many independent draws, shrinking the standard error of the ceiling estimate by ~sqrt(2) and directly attacking the documented stochastic-noise-floor obstacle. This is a CEILING-DOCUMENTATION move (toward the iter-20 mandate of *documenting* why this ceiling holds), not a ceiling-raising move: I do NOT expect hr to move off ~0 (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). HYPOTHESIS: at val_n=12 the mean SSIM lands near ~0.50-0.51 (the ep12/lr1e-4 peak family) with a TIGHTER read than the noisy val_n=6 single-seed numbers, giving a more-trustworthy ~0.51 ceiling estimate for the U-Net N2I on this synthetic 128-view substrate. FALSIFIER: if the val_n=12 mean lands FAR from 0.51 (e.g. <0.46 or >0.55), the val_n=6 set was itself unrepresentative and the ceiling claim needs the wider val set as its basis going forward. NOTE: val_n changes the absolute SSIM's comparability to iters 1-9 (different/larger scene set) -- that is the POINT (a cleaner, less-noisy basis), and it is recorded here so future iters read val_n=12 numbers against THIS iter, not the val_n=6 history. WALL: warm 12x200=2400 (unchanged) + per-image 12x600=7200 = 9600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 800 s, under the outer_wall_s=1200 guard and the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall (per_scene_s = 1200/12 = 100 s each, ample for 600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 50 s). All other knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-5 PEAK config (train_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16); ONLY val_n 6 -> 12 changed.

advice_for_others: diffusion_recon_dcstep_constrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=25, recon_eta=1.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=5, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-2 search-20260619-01 CONSTRAINED diff-recon. ONE KNOB: recon_eta 30.0->1.0 (DPS guidance gain). iter-1 (eta=30) = SSIM 0.3937 / hr 0.0 / PSNR 14.31 / RMSE 0.00963 — FAR BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor, i.e. the recon is corrupted relative to its own FBP init, not merely prior-dominated drift. Failure mode: the DPS step is adaptively normalized in-solver (step = (eta/||resid||)*grad, Chung 2023 eq.12), so eta is a dimensionless gain whose literature/demo/breast default is 1.0; eta=30 (a discarded-614 boundary-metric hint) is a 30x overshoot that, with recon_eta_clamp=false (no per-step displacement cap), blows the FBP-initialized iterate off-manifold every reverse step, and the relax=1.0 hard-DC then re-noises a corrupted x0. HYPOTHESIS: lowering eta 30->1 lets the DPS correction be a gentle pull, recovering SSIM from 0.39 toward/above the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.39-0.5 (still <<FBP) at eta=1, the DPS step size was NOT the issue — the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is mismatched to rebinned Mayo under the 25-step low-T budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful under DPS/DC) -> iter-3 redirects to the prior, not the DC weight. BUDGET: eta is free (no per-slice cost change); iter-1 ran 214 slices in 1018.96 s = 4.76 s/slice = 17.0 min < 20-min wall (1800s in-solver backstop never hit). val=ALL 214 L277, 321px geometry FOV default.

advice_for_others: diffusion_recon_dcstep_constrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=25, recon_eta=1.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=5, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=0.3, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-3 search-20260619-01 CONSTRAINED diff-recon. ONE KNOB: recon_dcstep_relax 1.0->0.3 (the constrained-specific hard-CG blend; eta held at iter-2's 1.0). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 eta=30 SSIM 0.3937/hr0; iter-2 eta 30->1 REGRESSED to SSIM 0.2366/hr0 -> eta is the WRONG lever (gentling the DPS gain did not help; the corruption is elsewhere). FAILURE MODE (numbers): both prior iters ran recon_dcstep_relax=1.0 = FULL hard projection. In dc_step_cg() the return is relax*x_cg + (1-relax)*x0_mu; relax=1.0 discards the diffusion x0 estimate ENTIRELY and substitutes n_cg=3 Gauss-Newton least-squares fit to the NOISY 2304-view LD sinogram, which is then re-noised back to t_next every 5 reverse steps (warmup 5). That least-squares fit overfits measurement noise and overwrites the prior's structure -> hard-CG DC re-noises a corrupted x0, exactly the constrained variant's failure. The SOLVER DEFAULT is relax=0.5; relax=1.0 was an untested aggressive choice carried from iter-1. ONE KNOB: relax 1.0->0.3 blends 30% CG-projected + 70% diffusion x0, a GENTLE pull to data consistency that preserves prior structure instead of overwriting it. HYPOTHESIS: softening the hard-DC blend lifts SSIM back toward / above the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor (hr>0); predicted iter-3 SSIM 0.4-0.7 range (recovery from 0.2366). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays well below FBP (~0.3 vs 0.81) even at relax=0.3, the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is STRUCTURALLY MISMATCHED to rebinned Mayo under the 25-step low-T DPS/DC budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful) -> NEGATIVE RESULT, STOP diffusion on Mayo. ONE KNOB: recon_dc_solver legacy->cg (NEW config-gated correct DC path in solver_diffusion_recon.py; legacy path byte-for-byte preserved + reproducible for all prior cfgs). The audit found the legacy DC-step is (1) a MISLABELED steepest-descent dressed as CG (dc_step_cg lines ~83-100) and (2) a re-injection that recomputes x0 from a STALE eps via x0_from_eps(x,eps,ab_next) then re-noises with a FRESH randn mid-schedule (lines ~162-174) — this collapsed unconstrained iter-4 to SSIM 0.055 and kept the constrained variant stuck 0.24-0.66 << the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor at hr=0. THE FIX (ported from the corrected solver_fast_recon.cg_data_consistency): recon_dc_solver=cg swaps in a GENUINE Fletcher-Reeves CG solve of AtA x = At y (residual + conjugate direction + FR beta), forms x0 from the CURRENT step's eps (x0_hat at t_now, not a stale eps re-eval'd at the wrong alpha_bar), CG-projects it, then re-embeds at t_next DETERMINISTICALLY as sqrt(ab_next)*x0_proj_norm + sqrt(1-ab_next)*eps_pred reusing the SAME eps (eps-prediction => the level-t noise direction IS eps_pred) — NO fresh randn, NO stale eps. BASE = iter-5 BEST (T=40, eta=30, relax=1.0, every5/n_cg3/warmup5, val_n=120, SSIM 0.6647/hr0 — the run-best constrained config). Hard DC stays ON (recon_dcstep_every=5) now that it is CORRECT. HONEST EXPECTATION: the corrected CG-DC should STOP the legacy re-noise corruption and likely RAISE SSIM above iter-5's 0.6647 (the deterministic same-eps re-embed no longer overwrites the trajectory with fresh noise + a least-squares fit to the noisy 2304-view LD sinogram). But on DENSE rebinned Mayo (LD-FBP near-complete at 2304 views) the v4 DDPM prior is regime-bounded, so hr may STILL be ~0 — the real payoff is the 128-view SPARSE benchmarks + the planned EMA v5 prior. FAILURE MODE: the recon is dominated by a Mayo v4 DDPM prior that is MISMATCHED to the rebinned-Mayo distribution under the short 25-step low-T reverse budget -- per findings the prior is globally faithful (plausible CT texture) but NOT conditionally faithful to the input sino under DPS/DC (exactly the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict, where 4x-16x capacity + 2.5x training all stayed in the 0.3-0.5 SSIM band). advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=1, pretrain_steps=20, n_iter=30, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_kernel=7, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, batch_size=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, outer_wall_s=1050, per_scene_s=None, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 feasibility (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). SOLVER: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i = PER-IMAGE Noise2Inverse with a trainable bilateral-filter stack (6 params: proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1, 3 sigma each), self-supervised, warm-start pre-pass + per-scan fit. STAYS PER-IMAGE (warm-start amortized pre-pass on the 4 train patients to capture a generic BF-sigma init, then an INDEPENDENT per-scan Adam fit on EACH val slice OWN half-angle measurements, GT-free; NEVER revert to amortized train-then-forward). HARD-WIRED path (baked into solver/loader/evaluate_calibrated, NOT cfg keys): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry (sod 595.362 / sdd 1086.803 / det_spacing 1.285044 / ps 0.700857), per-sample-ps half-angle projector swap (pipe.R_half per slice), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices, metric=321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). SIX-BOX: (1) iter-1 baseline -- does per-image bilateral N2I run on Mayo at all under the corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric and record a finite val_score+comparison.png within the 20-min budget. (2) FAILURE MODE: 214 INDEPENDENT per-scan fits (each backprops the 2304-view FBP adjoint) blow the 20-min wall -- the breast/demo bilateral N2I runs fit only 16-24 scenes in ~4-23 min; 214 is ~9-13x worse, and the U-Net DD-C run timed out at 24 scenes/25 min. (3) MINIMAL-COST per-image bilateral config: per-scan n_iter=30 (cheap), warm-start short (pretrain_steps=20 cap, 1 ep), mid bilateral depth proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1 at Wagner abdomen sigma defaults (kernel 5/7), grad_clip=1.0 MANDATORY (the 2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise), in-solver outer_wall_s=1050 so it RECORDS even if not all 214 finish. (4) HYPOTHESIS: per-image bilateral N2I is FBP-bounded + budget-starved at 214 slices -> expect hr near 0 (at/below LD-FBP), because half-view N2I info loss < full-view FBP and the warm-start fixes the structural ceiling; the 6-param bilateral physically CANNOT overfit a scan so it may edge out the U-Net N2I on a clean read. (5) BUDGET MATH (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score): anchored on Mayo bilateral N2I smoke 764666 (n_iter=40, val_n=2, per-image loop elapsed 10.3s => ~5.15 s/scene => ~0.129 s/(iter*scene) on the 2304-view adjoint; ~2x cheaper than the U-Net N2I 9.8 s/scene). At n_iter=30: 214*30*0.129 ~= 828s (13.8 min) + ~100s fixed startup (build 4 per-ps projectors + 214-slice LD-FBP baseline + score-214 + figure) ~= 16 min, fits inside 20-min with margin. n_iter=40 would be ~18.4 min + fixed ~= 20 min (too tight, risks the wall); n_iter=20 ~= 11 min (safe but gives the BF sigmas fewer steps to settle from warm-start). Chose n_iter=30 as the sane mid-cost; bilateral cannot overfit so more steps do not hurt. outer_wall_s=1050 (17.5 min) in-solver backstop guarantees a recorded result even if some slices run long; val stays ALL 214 (do NOT reduce val_n). (6) Do NOT return control mid-campaign.

advice_for_others: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=1, pretrain_steps=20, n_iter=30, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, proj_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.0005, img_kernel=7, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, batch_size=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, outer_wall_s=1050, per_scene_s=None, seed=42, rationale=iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: proj_sr 0.02 -> 0.0005 (projection-domain bilateral range sigma, 40x tighter). PER-IMAGE preserved (warm-start pre-pass + independent per-scan fit on each L277 slice OWN half-angle measurements, GT-free; NEVER amortized). SIX-BOX. (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.9248 (HIGHEST raw SSIM of any Mayo inference solver) but headroom=0.0 -- below the LD-FBP baseline on the calibrated RMSE-sensitive metric; elapsed 940.4s = 15.67 min; per-scan 940.4/214 = 4.39 s/scene at n_iter=30 (~0.131 s/(iter*scene) on the 2304-view FBP adjoint). (2) FAILURE MODE: high SSIM + hr~0 = the projection-domain bilateral OVER-SMOOTHS across attenuation edges (range sigma proj_sr=0.02 too loose for the 2304-view dense Mayo sinogram), washing out fine structure so RMSE rises even as global SSIM stays high -- same signature as dual_domain_bilateral_supervised (raw SSIM 0.919 highest yet hr only 0.028). (3) ONE KNOB justified: campaign-state lever insight (line 145) -- on Mayo (2304-view) the IMAGE-domain sigma is INERT and proj_sr-DOWN is the documented over-smoothing lever; tightening the projection range kernel preserves attenuation edges -> lower RMSE -> lift hr off the floor. Step 0.02->0.0005 matches the established breast sibling step (breast iter-08 proj_sr 0.02->0.0005). proj_sr is a sigma INIT, not a compute knob: kernel/n_iter/214-scans/FBP-adjoint cost all UNCHANGED, so the 20-min budget is identical to iter-1 (~940s = 15.7 min, ~260s slack inside 1200s) -- zero budget risk. (4) HYPOTHESIS: tightening proj_sr sharpens the projection-domain edge preservation -> RMSE drops -> hr rises above 0. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr stays ~0 with proj_sr=0.0005, the 6-param bilateral CAPACITY CEILING (not range-sigma tuning) is the limit on dense-view Mayo -- half-view N2I info loss < full-view LD-FBP and no sigma setting recovers it; that retires proj_sr as a lever and the next probe is img_n_bf depth. (5) HARD 20-min budget; val=ALL 214 L277 slices (NOT reduced); PER-IMAGE preserved; in-solver outer_wall_s=1050 (17.5 min) backstop guarantees a recorded result. (6) Do NOT return control mid-campaign.

advice_for_others: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=40, batch_size=4, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1080, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY under the corrected protocol (val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget). Hammernik-2017 here is an IMAGE-DOMAIN variational net that denoises the FBP -- NO projector inside the unrolled loop, so each forward is far cheaper than LPD (which ran the PYRO-NN projector in-loop and still did train200+score214 in 1149s/19.2min). That cheapness is spent on CONVERGENCE not capacity, to dodge the LPD trap (under-trained heavy unrolled net -> hr=0 @ SSIM 0.843). Capacity modest: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default for a cheaper RBF activation loop), vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31; vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 = the documented VN-port working corner (LOOSE hint, not validated). Training favors convergence: epochs=40, train_n=200, batch=4, lr=5e-4, grad_clip=1.0; max_train_s=1080 (18min) in-solver wall trips before the 30min SLURM kill, leaving headroom for score(214)+figure. Hyp: a budget-sized, ACTUALLY-CONVERGED Hammernik-2017 lands near or above the ~0.84 LD-FBP-ish SSIM floor within 20 min on Mayo; if even at 40 epochs it stays stuck at hr=0 with lambda_t barely budging (the documented 2026-06-08 failure signature), that is the iter-1 feasibility finding -- a shared-filter-bank structural ceiling, not a config knob away.

advice_for_others: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY (corrected protocol: val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-step model.projector swap, bg_target=truth, no fov= override). Hammernik-VN = MRI variational net ported to CT: T untied unrolled steps, each = learned filter-bank + per-filter RBF activation (the _rho_prime bump loop) PLUS an in-loop PYRO-NN projector data-consistency step (architectural twin of LPD/ItNet but tiny interpretable regulariser). CRITICAL LESSON from the SIBLING hammernik_2017 iter-1: it did NOT diverge to 0.0 -- it CUDA-OOM'd in _rho_prime at 72s with batch_size=4 (16GB RTX5000; the (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF tensors + 5-step autograd blew the card). So the dominant iter-1 risk here is MEMORY, not divergence. MITIGATION: batch_size=2 (NOT 4), vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default -> fewer RBF tensors), vn_checkpoint=true (gradient-checkpoints each unrolled step -- hammernik_vn HAS this knob, cuts activation memory ~T-fold; this is the key difference that lets the projector-in-loop VN fit where the 2017 batch=4 did not). STABILITY against the documented VN family divergence/NaN->0.0 trap: grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY -- the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward; clip_and_step also SKIPS nonfinite-gradient batches so a poisoned step can't collapse the recon to a constant), vn_dc_norm=true (power-iter normalizes R^T(Rx-g) so softplus(lambda_t) stays O(1) regardless of geometry -- the safeguard the projector-less 2017 lacked), lr=5e-4 (the documented hammernik_vn optimum from the discarded run; 8e-4 was worse, brief caps lr<=5e-4), vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 (loose VN-port working-corner hint). CAPACITY conservative per brief: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0 (FBP recon is ~O(1) so the RBF grid [-1,1] covers it). BUDGET: reference -- LPD (projector-in-loop, T=7, ep30, train200, score214) ran 1150s/19.2min right at the edge; hammernik_vn at T=5/N_k=16/checkpointed should be comparable-or-cheaper per step. max_train_s=1000 (16.7min in-solver wall) is the BINDING constraint (epochs=14 is just an upper bound the wall trips first), leaving ~3min for score(214)+figure under the 30min SLURM kill. HYPOTHESIS: if I run a budget-sized, MEMORY-SAFE (batch=2, checkpointed), STABLE (grad_clip=1.0, dc_norm) Hammernik-VN, I expect (a) it AVOIDS the hammernik_2017 OOM and produces a FINITE val_ssim within 20min, and (b) the projector DC step lands it near or above the ~0.84 LD-FBP SSIM floor -- because a learned-regulariser + true-projector-DC unroll is a sound Mayo recon family (sibling LPD/ItNet/DD-sup all run finite here). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric VN baseline that iter-2+ tunes one knob at a time (epochs/wall first to confirm convergence, then vn_T or vn_lambda_init).

LAST-LEVER / confirmation iter. ONE KNOB on the REGULARIZER (not capacity, not lambda): vn_normalize_filters False -> True (constrain each learned filter K_i to zero-mean + unit-norm, the paper-faithful constraint, solver _effective_weight lines 119-128). All else held at iter-3 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_lambda_init=0.05, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, all BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (vn_n_filters=16, elapsed 1295.7s); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (vn_n_filters=24, capacity UP -> REGRESSED -0.0133, elapsed 1351.7s); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05, DC-weight ~22x UP -> REGRESSED -0.0238, elapsed 1159.6s, val_psnr 32.07, val_rmse 1.246e-3). BOTH structural levers already attacked the wrong thing: capacity-UP regressed AND DC-weight-UP regressed, so the recon sits monotonically BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). FAILURE MODE (well-characterized): the learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i u) is a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline, and it does so REGARDLESS of capacity (filters^ hurt) or DC weight (lambda^ hurt). This FIRES iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier: 'if SSIM stays <=0.84 under strong DC, the VN regulariser is structurally degrading -> iter-4 attacks the regulariser itself: vn_normalize_filters=True OR vn_init=backproj'. CHOICE OF KNOB (most diagnostic remaining): vn_normalize_filters=True is the SHARPEST test of the smoothing diagnosis, and is preferred over vn_init=backproj (which changes only the init, not the regularizer mechanism, and the baseline is pinned to FBP either way). MECHANISM: zero-mean filters have NO DC response -- conv with a zero-mean kernel annihilates any uniform/low-frequency level component -- so a zero-mean-unit-norm-constrained K_i CANNOT apply a uniform smoothing or level shift to the image; the regulariser term can only act on local CONTRAST (edges/texture). Unit-norm caps each filter's gain so no single filter can dominate and over-smooth. If the iter-1/2/3 degradation was the unconstrained filters collapsing to a DC/low-pass smoother, this constraint removes that failure path -> the recon should stop sinking below the FBP init and hr should rise toward / above 0. HYPOTHESIS: with zero-mean unit-norm filters the regulariser stops smoothing the FBP init below baseline; val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr > 0). FALSIFIER (the terminal one): if val_ssim still <= 0.84 (below FBP) with the regulariser CONSTRAINED, then hammernik_vn is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on rebinned Mayo regardless of regulariser config (capacity, DC weight, AND filter constraint all exhausted) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT: the Hammernik-VN learned-regulariser family does not beat LD-FBP on real 2304-view Mayo LDCT, and drive the remaining iters to document the ceiling, not chase it. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the zero-mean/unit-norm normalization is a cheap per-step reshape (filter tensor is (24,1,11,11)); per-step forward/back-project DC cost is IDENTICAL to iter-3, so wall ~= iter-3 (1159.6s) -- well under the 1800s SLURM kill, ~640s margin. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-3 -- batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=24 within the 16 GB RTX5000 (no OOM; cf. the hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM at 72s). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise).

ONE KNOB (UNROLLED DEPTH, the last untested architectural axis): vn_T 5 -> 8. BASE = iter-1 BEST config (vn_n_filters=16, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_normalize_filters=False, train_n=200; NOT the regressed iter-2/3/4 and NOT iter-5 train_n=480). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, ALL <= the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor, baseline_PSNR 34.08): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (N_k=16, lam=0.0023, vn_T=5, 1295.7s) <- prior BEST-structural; iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (N_k 16->24 capacity^ REGRESSED -0.0133); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05 DC^ REGRESSED -0.0238); iter-4 SSIM 0.73363 (vn_normalize_filters F->T REGRESSED -0.0346); iter-5 SSIM 0.80886 PSNR 32.45 RMSE 1.192e-3 (train_n 200->480 data-coverage -> +0.0036 vs iter-1, but still <0.84, hr 0) <- run-BEST. LIMITER = REGULARISER-DEGRADATION, not under-training: loss flat by ep3 EVERY iter (vs the SIBLING hammernik_2017 which WAS under-trained -- epochs^ cleared ITS floor to hr 0.0375 at iter-7; hammernik_vn has NO such epoch headroom, loss is already converged). The learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho_prime_i(K_i u) acts as a BLUNT SMOOTHER dragging the FBP init below baseline. Capacity (filters), DC-weight (lambda), filter-constraint, AND data-coverage (train_n) are now ALL exhausted -- each either regressed or barely moved. The ONE architectural axis untouched across all 5 iters is the UNROLLED DEPTH vn_T (held =5 every iter). MECHANISM: each unrolled step t applies u <- u - K^T rho_prime - lam*R^T(Ru-g)/dc_norm, i.e. an in-loop PYRO-NN projector data-consistency step. More steps (T 5->8) means the true-projector DC term re-anchors the recon to the MEASURED sinogram 8 times instead of 5 -- the only mechanism in this architecture that can COUNTERACT the per-step regulariser smoothing (the DC pull, applied more often, fights the blunt-smoother regulariser). HYPOTHESIS: with vn_T 5->8 the extra projector-DC re-anchoring lifts val_ssim above the run-best 0.80886 toward the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER (terminal): if val_ssim stays <= 0.81 (still <FBP, hr=0) even at deeper unrolling, hammernik_vn is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on rebinned 2304-view Mayo LDCT with ALL architectural axes exhausted (capacity, DC-weight, filter-constraint, data-coverage, AND depth) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT and drive the remaining iters to DOCUMENT the ceiling toward iter-20, not chase it. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): vn_T 5->8 = 1.6x per-step DC+RBF cost. iter-1 ran ~7 ep/1000s at train_n=200,vn_T=5 (~143 s/ep) => at vn_T=8 ~229 s/ep => max_train_s=1000 trips at ~4.4 ep (>3, past the ep3 convergence point -> the converged comparison is fair). train_n REVERTED 480->200 (iter-5 coverage gain was a marginal +0.0036; at train_n=480+vn_T=8 the per-ep ~550s gives <2 ep -> would NOT converge). val_n=214 kept. Total ~= 1000 (train wall) + ~165 (score 214 + figure) ~= 1165s, under the 1800s SLURM kill (~635s margin). MEMORY-SAFE: vn_T=8 x N_k=16 but vn_checkpoint=true gradient-checkpoints each of the 8 unrolled steps (activation memory ~constant in T, NOT 8x) + batch_size=2 keep it within the 16 GB RTX5000 (cf. hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM at 72s). grad_clip=1.0 + vn_dc_norm=true retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward, and a deeper unroll makes the clip MORE load-bearing).

SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) PRIOR RESULTS: iter-1 ep8 -> SSIM 0.4413 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 20.44 / RMSE 0.004756, elapsed 191.1s; iter-2 ep48 -> SSIM 0.5927 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 24.77 / RMSE 0.002886, elapsed 387.4s. The pretrain_epochs lever moves SSIM (0.4413->0.5927, +0.151 over 8->48 ep) but hr stays PINNED at 0.000 -- v1 is still BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor after a 6x pretrain increase. CONTRAST: the lever-twin itnet_v2 (same pretrain-then-DC family) climbed ep48 0.5888 -> ep144 0.6230 (3x epochs for only +0.034 SSIM, hr still 0.000 -- severe diminishing returns), while the END-TO-END-trained sibling itnet_v3 sits at 0.905 / hr 0.312 at iter-3. v1 (0.44->0.59) and v2 (0.59->0.62) trace the SAME under-0.81 curve; v3 (0.91) is on a different curve entirely. (2) LIMITER = the pretrain-then-FIXED-DC CEILING (structural, confirmed by reading solver_itnet.py): finetune_itnet() is DEFINED (lines 114-135) but NEVER called in main(); the k=3 ItNet DC unroll (forward, lines 76-90) has ZERO trainable parameters of its own (self.alpha is a plain float, self.projector is fixed analytic PYRO-NN); itnet.eval()+torch.no_grad() (lines 208-209) run the unroll as pure INFERENCE. The ONLY trainable component is the standalone SmallUNet denoiser (params_M=0.2329, exactly the UNet), pretrained as an FBP->truth denoiser that NEVER sees the DC steps during training. So pretrain_epochs is the sole lever and the fixed untrained DC post-processor caps v1 far below the end-to-end v3. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48 -> 160 (3.3x), mirroring v2's 48->144 ceiling-probe escalation. The counter-hypothesis (v1 suddenly clears 0.81 at 160 ep) is implausible given the +0.151 then +0.034-class diminishing slope already measured. CONFIG: residual_learning=False (MANDATORY: the CONFIG default True double-applies the residual -- SmallUNet.forward already returns x-body(x), then ItNetV2.forward re-adds denoiser(x) -> ~2x at eval which the k DC steps cannot recover, stuck ~0.34; False matches the working v1/v3 recipe). Shared ItNet architecture seeded from itnet_v3 iter-1 (0.896 SSIM / hr0.268 under the SAME corrected metric): itnet_k=3 DC steps, unet_c=16 SmallUNet denoiser, itnet_alpha_init=0.0037 (TV-lambda, learnable), grad_clip=1.0 (mandatory: 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside dc_step overflows otherwise), seed=42. TRAINING uses v2 pretrain knobs (v2 pre-trains the denoiser then applies k=3 DC at eval; it is NOT end-to-end like v3): pretrain_lr=1e-4 (v3 unstable above; mirror), pretrain_epochs=12, pretrain_patience=12 (disable the 1pct early-stop so the full budget converges -- AVOID the v1 0.441 under-training trap). batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 are FORCED by per-sample-ps (each slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps). train_n=200 -> 200 steps/epoch. val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices -- do NOT reduce). max_train_s=900 (15 min) HARD backstop so train leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the 30-min wall. HYPOTHESIS: itnet_v2 with residual_learning=False at k=3/c=16/lr=1e-4 for 12 pretrain epochs on 200 stratified Mayo train slices produces a finite val_ssim that CLEARS the LD-FBP baseline (hr>0) and lands in the ~0.88-0.90 SSIM band like its siblings, because a pretrained denoiser + k=3 DC-step refinement of the per-sample-ps FBP is a strong Mayo recon family and the residual_learning=False fix removes the double-residual collapse. This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric baseline that iter-2+ will improve by tuning ONE knob (pretrain_epochs first).

advice_for_others: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, itnet_alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.0001, pretrain_epochs=48, pretrain_patience=48, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=960, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 12->48 (4x); pretrain_patience tracked 12->48 so the early-stop never fires before the full 48 epochs (same disable-early-stop intent as iter-1, where patience==epochs). All else identical to iter-1 (k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=1e-4, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); only max_train_s 900->960 to admit the longer pretrain inside the wall. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 (val_psnr 21.24, val_rmse 0.00434) in elapsed_s=170.2 -- only ~14% of the 1200s (20-min) train+score budget used; pretrain_epochs=12. (2) FAILURE MODE: the pretrain-denoiser-then-data-consistency path UNDER-CONVERGES in the budget (same as v1, which was stuck at 0.441). The k=3 DC steps refine a denoiser that has not yet learned the Mayo image statistics; SSIM 0.455 is far below the end-to-end itnet_v3 sibling (0.896). With only 12 pretrain epochs at lr=1e-4 the denoiser is under-trained, and 170s/1200s proves the budget was almost entirely idle. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 12->48, mirroring the SIBLING itnet (v1) iter-2 which raised pretrain_epochs 8->48 and jumped SSIM 0.441->0.593 (+0.15) under THIS campaign and metric -- the strongest just-proven signal that pretraining was the v1/v2 bottleneck. Chosen over lr-up (v3 is unstable above 1e-4; mirror the safe v1 move) and over architecture knobs (k/unet_c) which would change the model not the convergence. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if pretrain_epochs 12->48, val_ssim rises substantially above 0.4554 (toward v1 iter-2's ~0.59, possibly the ~0.88-0.90 sibling band) because more pretraining lets the denoiser converge before the k=3 DC refinement, exactly as it did for v1. FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays flat (<=~0.47) at 48 epochs, the pretrain-DC architecture is CAPPED in this budget regardless of pretraining (not an under-training problem), and iter-3 must move toward end-to-end unrolled training (the v3 recipe) or accept the pretrain-DC path is budget-limited. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. iter-1 ran 12 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 170s; the per-epoch pretrain cost over 200 stratified slices is the variable part and the 214-slice per-sample val + figure are roughly fixed. 4x the epochs is roughly 4x the small pretrain base plus the single fixed val/figure pass: est well under 600s, far below 1200s; max_train_s=960 is a 16-min HARD backstop so train always leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged from iter-1): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (each slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps; batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override). residual_learning=False KEPT (the CONFIG default True double-applies the residual and collapses eval to ~0.34).
