ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48->144 (3x); pretrain_patience tracked 48->144 so early-stop never fires before the full run (same disable-early-stop intent as iter-1/iter-2 where patience==epochs). All else identical to iter-2 (k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=1e-4, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); only max_train_s 960->1100 (18.3-min HARD backstop) to admit the longer pretrain inside the 20-min train+score budget while leaving the figure outside. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 @pretrain_epochs=12 in elapsed_s=170.2; iter-2 = SSIM 0.5888 / hr 0.000 @pretrain_epochs=48 in elapsed_s=345.2. Trajectory: 4x epochs (12->48) lifted SSIM +0.133, still hr=0 (FBP floor ~0.81, far above). v3 SIBLING (same ItNet family, END-TO-END unrolled, no pretrain-DC) reaches SSIM 0.91 -- the contrast that frames v2's limiter. Budget: iter-2 used only 345s of the 1200s (20-min) budget (~29%) -- large headroom remains; the variable (pretrain) part was ~233s, fixed (214-slice per-sample val + figure) ~112s. (2) LIMITER: pretrain-DC UNDER-CONVERGENCE -- and structurally deeper: reading solver_itnet_v2.py, the DC stage is NOT trained at all. pretrain_denoiser trains ONLY the SmallUNet on (fbp, truth) residual pairs; ItNetV2 is then built and itnet.eval() runs with NO fine-tune of the unrolled net -- log_alpha (the DC step size) is never optimized, so the k=3 DC refinement is a FIXED, untrained operator wrapped around a pretrained denoiser. That is why v2 caps far below the end-to-end v3 (0.91): more pretraining only sharpens the denoiser, it cannot fix the un-trained DC coupling. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48->144 (3x) -- the most diagnostic single knob to MAP the pretrain-epochs response curve and definitively decide whether the cap is epochs or architecture. Chosen over a DC-stage knob (itnet_k / itnet_alpha_init) because the DC stage carries no trainable weight (changing k/alpha shifts a fixed operator, not a learnable one -- low diagnostic value), and over lr-up (v3 unstable above 1e-4; mirror the safe sibling move). With a fixed-DC architecture, pretrain_epochs is the ONLY lever that can lift the denoiser, so pushing it 3x is the cleanest test of the ceiling. (4) HYPOTHESIS + FALSIFIER: if pretrain_epochs 48->144 lands val_ssim still ~0.59-0.65 (NOT the ~0.91 v3 band), then itnet_v2's pretrain-then-FIXED-DC scheme is STRUCTURALLY CAPPED on Mayo regardless of epochs -- the un-trained DC operator, not under-training, is the limiter -- and the campaign should treat v2 as a documented budget/architecture ceiling and use v3 instead. CONVERSELY if SSIM jumps substantially toward the sibling band, the cap was pretrain-epochs and iter-4 keeps climbing. The diminishing 12->48 (+0.133) vs the still-large gap to 0.81/0.91 predicts the former (structural cap). (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. Per-epoch ~4.86s over 200 stratified slices (from iter-1->iter-2 slope) -> 144 ep ~700s pretrain + ~112s fixed val+figure ~812s, comfortably under 1200s and the 30-min sbatch wall; max_train_s=1100 is the HARD backstop so train always leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. ONE KNOB: train_n 400->579 (FULL 579-slice train pool, ~69%->100% coverage), with pretrain_epochs traded 120->72 + pretrain_patience tracked 120->72 (early-stop stays disabled) to HOLD the HARD 1200s wall AND keep grad-step parity train_n*epochs (iter-7 400*120=48000; iter-8 579*72=41688, ~13% fewer steps as a budget-safety margin since iter-7 overran at 1308.6s). MECHANISM (campaign_state.md, CONFIRMED): build_dataset calls load_val_split(split='train', n=train_n) -> a FIXED n-slice subset loaded ONCE; pretrain_denoiser merely reshuffles that subset each epoch (torch.randperm), NO RotatingSubsetDataset. CURRENT train_n=400 (~69% of 579 pool). (2) LIMITER: with itnet_k=1 unlocked, the binding limiter is now the TRAINED DENOISER's data coverage -- it only sees ~69% of the anatomy in the 579-slice pool because the fixed-subset loader never rotates. The single trained-denoiser+1-DC pass is excellent (0.9414) but the denoiser is data-coverage-limited, the proven climb lever for the end-to-end/denoiser trainers this campaign. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 400->579 (full pool), pretrain_epochs traded 120->72 to hold budget; itnet_k=1 KEPT, residual_learning=False KEPT. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if train_n 400->579, val_ssim/hr rises ABOVE iter-7 0.4187 because the denoiser sees 100% vs 69% of the 579-slice anatomical variety at near-equal optimization, exactly as full-coverage lifted uswin/itnet_v3/v1. NUMERIC FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.4187 (flat/down) at train_n=579, the denoiser is NOT data-coverage-limited at k=1 -- coverage is exhausted -- and iter-9 reverts to tn400 and probes pretrain_epochs UP (more denoiser convergence) as the next lever. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score. iter-7 per-epoch at tn400/k1 ~8.31s/epoch, fixed (214-slice per-sample val + figure) ~312s (1308.6 - 120*8.31). At tn579 per-epoch ~8.31*579/400=12.03s/epoch -> 72 ep: 72*12.03 + 312 = 1178s, UNDER 1200s (and grad-steps 41688 < 48000 gives extra margin vs iter-7's overrun). max_train_s=1050 (17.5-min HARD backstop) GUARANTEES the 214-slice per-sample val + figure finish inside the 30-min sbatch wall, ending the overrun risk. val_n=214 KEPT (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT, batch_size=2 (itnet_v2 needs bs=2 per six-box) -- NOTE solver FORCES bs=1+val_chunk=1 via per-sample-ps so this is moot. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. advice_for_others: itnet_v3-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=24, alpha_init=0.0037, lr=0.0001, epochs=9, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=780, seed=42, rationale=iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). ONE KNOB: unet_c 16 -> 24 (CAPACITY), with epochs traded DOWN 18 -> 9 to fund the bigger net inside the HARD 20-min train+score wall. All else = iter-3 exactly (itnet_k=3, alpha_init=0.0037, lr=1e-4, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); max_train_s lowered 900 -> 780 as a tighter train backstop for the slower c=24 net. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 ep8 -> SSIM 0.895903 / hr 0.268409, elapsed 737.85s=12.30min; iter-2 ep14 -> SSIM 0.908534 / hr 0.310054, elapsed 1010.07s=16.83min; iter-3 ep18 -> SSIM 0.904773 / hr 0.312282, elapsed 1072.94s=17.88min. The epochs lever has PLATEAUED: iter-2 ep14 -> iter-3 ep18 gave hr +0.0022 only (0.310054 -> 0.312282) AND SSIM DROPPED (0.908534 -> 0.904773). iter-3's own falsifier (hr <= 0.310 at ep18 => capacity-limited) effectively FIRED -> itnet_v3 is CAPACITY-limited at unet_c=16, not training-convergence-limited. unet_c=16 is the current capacity; epochs=18 is the current count. (2) LIMITER NOW = model CAPACITY at c=16 (epochs plateaued AND iter-3 used 17.88/20 min so epochs cannot be raised further inside the wall anyway). (3) ONE KNOB: unet_c 16 -> 24 (params 3.70M -> ~8.3M, ~2.25x conv FLOPs). epochs traded DOWN 18 -> 9 to keep train+score inside 1200s. itnet_v3 is the END-TO-END unrolled variant (unlike v1/v2's pretrain-denoiser-then-DC), so added denoiser capacity is trained against the full recon objective and should genuinely lift the ceiling. (4) HYPOTHESIS: more denoiser capacity (c=24) lifts hr above 0.3123 even at only 9 epochs, because the c=16 net had saturated its representational headroom (ep14->18 flat). FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.3123 at c=24/ep9, itnet_v3 has hit its representational ceiling on this 214-slice val set (added capacity does not help OR 9 epochs is too few to train the bigger net) -> iter-5 must either give the bigger net more epochs (trade train_n down to buy them) or pivot to lr/itnet_k. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score), CAPACITY-vs-EPOCHS trade math: measured c=16 timing over 3 points (8,737.85),(14,1010.07),(18,1072.94) gives full-span per-epoch (1072.94-737.85)/(18-8)=33.5 s/epoch and fixed cost (data load + per-sample-ps projector cache + 214-slice per-sample val + figure + startup) 737.85-8*33.5=469.8 s. Raising c 16->24 scales the UNet conv FLOPs by (24/16)^2=2.25x, but the k=3 DC steps run the 2304-view projector fwd+adj which is FLAT in c, so per-epoch does NOT fully 2.25x. Conservative split (UNet ~half of per-epoch train, half is projector/data; only ~25pct of fixed is the c-scaling val UNet-forward): per-epoch@c24 ~= 52-60 s, fixed@c24 ~= 631 s. At epochs=9: 631 + 9*~56 = ~1135s = 18.9 min < 1200s even pessimistically (unet_share=0.6 case = 19.57 min, still OK); epochs=10 risks the wall in the pessimistic case (20.6 min), epochs=8 wastes headroom. So epochs=9 is the largest count that the c=24 timing safely permits inside 20 min. max_train_s=780 fences the train phase (9*~56=~504s expected, well under 780) so a finite recon + 214-slice val + figure always land inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside dc_step overflows otherwise). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-sample itnet.projector swap for the k=3 DC steps, bg_target=truth. (6) do NOT return control mid-campaign. Predicted iter-4 hr: 0.32-0.35 if capacity-limited hypothesis holds; <=0.3123 falsifies.

GOAL: does naf (Neural Attenuation Field, per-scene self-supervised INR -- one coordinate-MLP optimized PER L277 slice against its OWN sinogram, no training set) run on Mayo under the corrected path (staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, inlined single-val-ps probe -> reconstructs at L277 native ps ~0.73979, bg_target=truth) and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png within the HARD 20-min budget, scoring ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override)? BUDGET REASONING (the load-bearing decision): NAF has NO training (train_n=0); the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop, total = val_n x per_scene. val=ALL 214 L277 slices is MANDATORY (protocol; do NOT reduce). 18-min outer wall (naf_outer_wall_s=1080, inside the 20-min compute budget, leaving headroom for the figure+IO before the 30-min sbatch kill) / 214 scenes = naf_per_scene_s=5.0 s/scene. Mayo is 512x512 images at 2304 views x 736 channels, so each Adam step = a 512^2 MLP forward + a 2304-view fan-beam forward-project + backward = EXPENSIVE; 5 s/scene buys only a handful of steps (a NeRF-style fit wants hundreds-to-thousands). naf_n_iter=3000 is a HIGH CAP so the PER-SCENE WALL (t_limit in fit_one_scene), NOT the iter count, is the governor -- each scene runs as many steps as fit in 5 s. To squeeze the most out of the tiny budget: leaner MLP than default (hidden 192->128, layers 5->4, n_freqs 10->8 => cheaper steps => a few more fit per scene) and naf_lr 5e-3->1e-2 (with only a handful of steps, a higher lr converges faster from the water-mu init). naf_n_clip=0.05 (sigmoid head out_scale), naf_tv_weight=1e-4 defaults. HYPOTHESIS: NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT -- solver_plan.md flags NAF/R2G hr~0 on dense-view; the discarded boundary-slice run hinted naf 0.911 < LD-FBP ~0.81-cal baseline, a behavior hint only) AND it is BUDGET-STARVED on the 214-slice protocol (5 s/scene = far too few per-scene Adam steps for a NeRF-style convergence). Expect val_ssim that does NOT clear the LD-FBP baseline (hr near 0). The directive (a) was to implement the paper's radiative splat-to-detector renderer + Eq.7 rectification. FEASIBILITY VERDICT (in solver FAITHFUL_SPLAT_VERDICT): NOT a tractable net-positive iter here. (i) Rectification is a NO-OP for our forward model -- our solver rasterises the Gaussian mixture into a mu-image then applies PYRO-NN's EXACT discrete X-ray transform (unbiased line integral, no per-Gaussian normalization to omit); Zha's bias only arises in the splat-AND-SUM path, so raster-then-project ALREADY IS the unbiased operator the rectification recovers. (ii) A true 2D fan-beam splatter does NOT reuse PYRO-NN (which exposes only image<->sino on a fixed grid, no per-Gaussian detector-footprint primitive) and needs a custom differentiable EWA kernel -- hundreds of lines, far over the ~150-line one-iter bar. (iii) DECISIVE: the binding constraint is COMPUTE, not fidelity -- iters 1-5 (all hr=0, SSIM 0.68-0.74, all BELOW the 0.808 LD-FBP baseline) show the raster forward already costs ~0.282 s/Adam-step and only 10-64 of 214 slices complete in the 20-min wall; a per-Gaussian-per-view splatter is MORE expensive, so a faithful renderer would cover FEWER scenes and score WORSE. R2Gaussian is regime-bounded on dense 2304-view Mayo (hr~0 regardless); its real payoff is the 128-view SPARSE benchmarks. So I SCAFFOLDED gs_render=splat (config-gated, default raster, raises NotImplementedError) + wrote the verdict, and as the ACTUAL iter-6 take the directive's queued CHEAP in-budget lever (the iter+2 fix (b)): enable gs_init_from_fbp=True (was disabled) + add an SSIM loss term (gs_ssim_weight=0.1; benchmark is SSIM-scored). ONE COMPOUND LEVER from iter-1 BEST base (n_iter=150 / 512 Gaussians -- the config that produced the run-best SSIM 0.7383). FAILURE MODE iters 1-5: cold uniform-init Gaussians spend the scarce ~26 completed-scene budget refining a per-scene recon that lands BELOW its 0.808 FBP init, so the 214-average is dragged down by sub-FBP completed scenes. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): FBP warm-start (positions sampled proportional to fbp^2, amp seeded from FBP intensity) + an SSIM pull toward the FBP structure makes the ~26 completed scenes land AT/ABOVE their FBP init instead of below it, so the 214-avg rises toward the 0.808 FBP baseline (from iter-1 0.7383). PREDICTION: SSIM in (0.74, 0.81), hr most likely still 0 (regime-bounded: even matching FBP yields hr=0, and beating dense-Mayo FBP per-scene in 150 Adam steps is implausible). FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= 0.7383 (no lift over iter-1 best), warm-start+SSIM does not rescue the per-scene quality and the dense-Mayo structural ceiling stands -- file the negative result. BUDGET: gs_init_from_fbp adds ~0 per-step cost (init only); the SSIM term adds one cheap conv-SSIM per step vs the dominating 2304-view projection, so per-step stays ~0.282 s and coverage ~26/214 (same as iter-1); gs_outer_wall_s=1080 self-truncates before the SLURM kill, figure excluded, --time=00:30:00 has headroom. val_n stays 214 per mandate; staged_canonical/v3/per-sample-ps(single-val-ps probe)/bg_target=truth/321px-FOV-default all hard-wired. advice_for_others: ram_zeroshot-claude-agentic: ram_ckpt_path=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ram.pth.tar, ram_input_norm=adjoint_max, ram_clamp_output=True, ram_finetune=False, ram_finetune_epochs=0, ram_finetune_lr=0.0001, ram_disable_multiscale=True, ram_disable_cudnn=False, ram_use_deepinv_tomo=False, ram_sigma=0.005, ram_factor=0.2, ram_post_fbp_blend=0.3, val_n=214, rationale=iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol): ONE knob ram_factor 0.55->0.2 (all else at the iter-1 point: ram_post_fbp_blend BACK to 0.3, ram_sigma=0.005, adjoint_max norm, multiscale disabled, finetune OFF). Trajectory: iter-1 SSIM 0.8611 hr 0.0 (blend 0.3, factor 0.55); iter-2 SSIM 0.8644 hr EXACTLY 0.0 (blend 0.3->0.5) -- the FBP/RAM blend coefficient is EXHAUSTED: raising the FBP fraction lifted raw SSIM marginally (+0.003) but did NOT move calibrated headroom off 0.0, so on the RMSE-sensitive metric RAM is at/below the LD-FBP floor (baseline 0.8078, oracle HD-FBP 0.9331) regardless of blend. Failure mode: RAM is a pretrained zero-shot deepinv recon that never saw real LDCT helical-rebinned fan data; its denoiser adds no recoverable signal over FBP on dense (2304-view) rebinned Mayo -> FBP-bounded. ONE knob NOT yet probed = ram_factor (physics.factor, solver_ram.py L348), the operator-gain used in RAM's prox_l2 data-consistency realign step (L20: 0 = skip prox_l2). It is the most DIAGNOSTIC remaining RAM hyperparameter: blend mixes FBP vs RAM linearly AFTER inference, whereas ram_factor changes RAM's INTERNAL DC step -- the actual mechanism by which RAM is supposed to add signal over its FBP init. Lower it 0.55->0.2 (toward the skip-prox_l2 limit) to isolate whether weakening RAM's DC realign moves the metric at all. Hypothesis: RAM is structurally FBP-bounded on dense Mayo -- the prox_l2 strength does not matter because RAM's prior carries no LDCT-specific signal. Falsifier: if hr at ram_factor=0.2 != 0.0 (rises OR drops), RAM's internal DC step DOES matter and RAM is not purely FBP-bounded; if hr stays flat at 0.0 across both the post-hoc blend (iter-2) AND the internal prox_l2 gain (iter-3), RAM is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on dense Mayo -> FILE NEGATIVE RESULT, STOP iterating this solver. Budget: only a scalar physics.factor changes -> zero added compute vs iter-2 (which ran 1100.9 s = 18.3 min for 214 single forward passes + one op-norm power iter), inside the HARD 20-min train+score budget; sbatch --time=00:30:00 backstop wall. val_n stays 214 (score ALL L277 slices @ 321px detector-geometry FOV). HARD-WIRED: staged_canonical, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted, per-sample-ps, bg_target=truth, 321px FOV default.

SEMANTICS (solver_ram.py L15/L327/L346): ram_sigma is the Gaussian noise-level conditioning passed to physics.noise_model (dinv.physics.GaussianNoise(sigma=ram_sigma)) -- it tells the pretrained RAM denoiser HOW NOISY to treat the input, i.e. the prior STRENGTH, which is the core mechanism by which RAM is supposed to add recoverable signal beyond its FBP init. Raising it 4x (0.005->0.02) makes RAM denoise MORE aggressively -- the most aggressive single-knob test of whether the RAM prior carries ANY LDCT-specific recoverable signal at ANY strength. Trajectory under the corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric: iter-1 SSIM 0.8611 hr 0.0 (blend0.3/factor0.55/sigma0.005); iter-2 SSIM 0.8644 hr EXACTLY 0.0 (blend0.3->0.5 -- post-hoc linear FBP/RAM mix EXHAUSTED); iter-3 SSIM 0.8968 hr 0.0 (factor0.55->0.2 -- internal prox_l2 DC gain EXHAUSTED; weakening the DC realign RAISED raw SSIM +0.033 but kept calibrated headroom pinned at 0.0). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS, not CT pixels): (1) prev result: hr 0.0 on all of post-hoc blend AND internal prox_l2 gain; (2) FBP-bound named: RAM is a pretrained zero-shot deepinv recon that never saw real LDCT helical-rebinned 2304-view fan data; its denoiser prior adds no recoverable signal over FBP on dense Mayo -> the calibrated headroom is pinned at the LD-FBP floor (hr=0) regardless of which inference knob moves; (3) ONE knob: ram_sigma 0.005->0.02 (the last untried hyperparameter, the denoiser prior strength); (4) hypothesis: hr stays EXACTLY 0.0 -- the noise-conditioning does not matter because the RAM prior carries no LDCT-specific signal; predict hr 0; (5) falsifier: if hr at ram_sigma=0.02 != 0.0 (rises OR drops), RAM's denoiser strength DOES move the metric and RAM is NOT purely FBP-bounded; (6) verdict trigger: if hr stays 0.0 across the post-hoc blend (iter-2), the internal prox_l2 gain (iter-3), AND now the denoiser noise-conditioning (iter-4), RAM is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on dense Mayo across ALL three inference levers -> FILE FBP-BOUND NEGATIVE RESULT, STOP iterating this solver. advice_for_others: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: tv_clip_max 0.05->0.08 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-1: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). iter-1 NUMBERS: SSIM 0.922979, hr 0.132941, PSNR 35.32, RMSE 8.57e-4, elapsed 918s (15.3 of 20 min) -- already the best inference solver on Mayo, cleared baseline. FAILURE MODE: the hard upper clamp f.clamp_(0.0, clip_max) at 0.05 truncates every voxel above mu=0.05, i.e. it caps bone / high-attenuation structures; real Mayo LDCT attenuation exceeds 0.05, so bone detail is flattened. The headroom metric is RMSE-sensitive, so the truncated bone is a direct uncredited RMSE penalty. HYPOTHESIS: raising tv_clip_max 0.05->0.08 lets high-mu bone voxels through, so val_ssim and hr rise above iter-1 (0.923 / 0.133), because the 0.05 clamp was the binding upper constraint on bone and the RMSE-sensitive headroom was penalizing its truncation. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.133 (no gain or regression), the clamp is NOT the binding constraint at this lambda, and iter-3 must instead tune tv_lambda (the data-vs-smoothness balance). BUDGET: tv_clip_max is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- identical iteration count (120) -> identical ~918s wall, ~282s margin under the 1200s 20-min budget preserved. tv_iterations deliberately NOT raised: iter-1 used 918/1200s, so more iters would risk the wall (the failure mode iter-1 flagged). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.003, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: tv_lambda 0.001->0.003 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-2: tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). NUMBERS: iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08) elapsed 928s. Trajectory: the clip bump moved hr +0.072 (0.133->0.205) and dropped RMSE 8.3% by un-truncating high-mu bone -- the clamp WAS the binding constraint (iter-2 falsifier 'hr<=0.133' NOT triggered). iter-2 clip_max=0.08 is now at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] so clip is exhausted as a lever. tv_lambda has been FROZEN at the solver default 0.001 for BOTH prior iters -- never probed -- and is the highest-value untouched knob (the classical data-vs-smoothness balance). FAILURE MODE: Mayo is real LOW-DOSE CT where the dominant error is photon/electronic noise, not under-sampling (2304 views is dense). At lambda=0.001 the data term dominates: SSIM barely moves between iters (recon is data-fit-dominated, leaving the LDCT noise floor in), and the iter-1->2 headroom gain came PURELY from un-truncating bone (clip), NOT from denoising. The regularizer is currently too WEAK to suppress LDCT noise. HYPOTHESIS: raising tv_lambda 0.001->0.003 strengthens the TV denoiser, suppressing residual LDCT noise so val_rmse drops below 7.857e-4 and hr rises above 0.205364; the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower noise floor. 3x is a bounded probe inside [0.0001,0.01] -- large enough to move the needle, small enough not to over-smooth in one shot. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.205 (no gain or regression) either side of lambda=0.003, TV is AT its regularization ceiling on Mayo (lambda=0.001 was already near-optimal) -- the lever is exhausted and the next probe would be tv_lr/tv_iterations for finer convergence, or accept ~0.92 SSIM / ~0.20 hr as the structural TV ceiling on real Mayo LDCT. BUDGET: tv_lambda is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- identical iteration count (120) -> identical ~928s wall, ~272s margin under the 1200s hard 20-min budget preserved. tv_iterations deliberately NOT raised: iter-2 used 928/1200s, and lambda is the higher-value probe per the mandate. val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=160, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the iter-2 BEST config (clip 0.08, lambda 0.001), NOT iter-3's regressed lambda 0.003. ONE KNOB: tv_iterations 120->160 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-2: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) -- the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) -- REGRESSED, over-smoothed (lambda-up is exhausted). The two prior levers are SPENT: tv_clip_max is at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] (clip exhausted), and tv_lambda-up regressed in iter-3 (denoise-strength exhausted). The remaining untried lever is tv_iterations: it has been FROZEN at 120 for all 3 prior iters, deliberately conservative to protect the 20-min wall. OPPORTUNITY: is hr 0.205 ITERATIONS-LIMITED (the TV gradient descent has not fully converged at 120 steps, so the recon still has residual data-term error the schedule has not driven out) or is it at the TV REGULARIZATION CEILING (120 iters is already converged and 0.205 hr / ~0.924 SSIM is the structural TV limit on real Mayo LDCT)? FAILURE MODE TO AVOID: oversizing tv_iterations blows the HARD 20-min (1200s) wall on the 214-slice val pass. HYPOTHESIS: 33% more TV gradient-descent steps (120->160) from the iter-2 BEST config converge the recon further, lowering val_rmse below 7.857e-4 so hr rises above 0.205364 (the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual). FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.205 (no gain or regression at 160 iters), TV is at its regularization ceiling on Mayo (~0.924 SSIM / 0.205 hr) and 120 iters was already converged -- the iters lever is exhausted too, and the next probe would be tv_lr (finer convergence per step) or accept the structural TV ceiling. BUDGET: the cost model is T(n)=overhead + n*c_step. From iter-2's 928.5s at 120 iters and the iter-1 per-slice-iter rate (~0.018 s/slice-iter * 214 slices = 3.85 s/TV-iter), fixed overhead (214-slice load+FBP+per-iter scoring) ~= 466s. n=160 -> T ~= 466 + 160*3.85 ~= 1083s = 90% of the 1200s budget (~117s margin). Robustness: even at +10% step-cost variance (GPU contention) n=160 lands ~1144s, still under the wall; n=180 was REJECTED because at +10% variance it goes over (1229s). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.

ADDS a SHORT supervised training phase (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1) on top of the 214-slice val pass. BUDGET (HARD 20 min train+score): classical tv_iterative ran 120 GD-iters x 214 slices in 918s (~0.036 s/slice-iter, dominated by the 2304-view 512px projector pair). This variant: val = K=10 unrolled x 214 slices, val_chunk=5 -> ~80-120s. Train = 40 samples x 8 epochs x K=10 x (fwd+bwd, ~2-3x a val slice-iter) ~ 256-380s. + 214-slice FBP precompute + load ~120s. Total ~7-10 min, ~2x margin under the 1200s wall. bs=1 holds only one K-step autograd graph at a time (memory-safe on 16 GB; no OOM risk vs the hammernik bs=4 OOM). FAILURE MODES TO AVOID: (a) 214-slice TV recon x training blows the wall -> kept K, train_n, epochs conservative; (b) under-training the 20 scalars -> epochs=8 gives the learnable step/lambda schedule room to depart from the seed while still fitting. If it under-performs the classical baseline, the K=10 unrolled depth (vs classical 120 iters) is the limiter and iter-2 raises tv_K.

ONE KNOB CHANGED: tv_K 10 -> 30 (3x deeper unroll). All else identical to iter-1 (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, lr=5e-3, val_n=214 ALL L277 slices, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00 with 10-min figure/IO headroom): iter-1 ran K=10 in 321.5s. In reality a large slice of 321.5s is FIXED overhead (data load + 214-slice FBP precompute + per-ps probe ~60-120s), so the true K=30 cost is well under 964s. bs=1 holds only ONE K-step autograd graph at a time -> deeper K raises activation memory linearly but stays memory-safe on 16 GB (no OOM; cf. the hammernik bs=4 OOM). advice_for_others: uswin-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=214, epochs=64, batch_size=4, lr=0.0005, uswin_c=24, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=ITER-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). ONE KNOB: epochs 40 -> 64 (1.6x); everything else identical to iter-2 (train_n=200, val_n=214, bs=4, lr=5e-4, uswin_c=24, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=1000, seed=42). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) TRAJECTORY iter-1 ep10 -> SSIM 0.885910 / hr 0.173021 in 328.96s; iter-2 ep40 -> SSIM 0.914097 / hr 0.322063 in 737.72s. epochs-up lever CONFIRMED (hr +0.149 for +30 epochs, monotone, near-linear). iter-2 used 737.72s = 61pct of the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall -> clear epoch headroom. (2) LIMITER: still UNDER-TRAINED, not capacity/optimization-limited (hr rose monotonically with epochs, no sign of a convergence basin yet; uswin is historically epochs-sensitive, ep10->40 prior run 0.173->0.322). The new ceiling is the 20-min wall, not the optimizer. (3) ONE KNOB = epochs 40 -> 64, justified by timing: from the two measured (epochs, elapsed_s) points the per-epoch cost is (737.72-328.96)/(40-10)=13.63 s/epoch and the fixed cost (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure I/O) is 328.96-10*13.63=192.7s. Max epochs that fit the 1200s wall: (1200-192.7)/13.63=73.9 -> 64 predicts 192.7 + 64*13.63 = 1065s = 17.7 min (~135s margin inside the 1200s budget; sbatch wall is 30 min). ep72 would be 1174s = 19.6 min (only 26s margin -> too tight given timing variance), so 64 is chosen as the safe-aggressive count. Train-only = 64*13.63 = 872s < max_train_s=1000 backstop, so the backstop does NOT truncate training. (4) HYPOTHESIS: uswin is still epochs-limited at ep40; +60pct more gradient steps (40->64) lifts hr above the iter-2 0.322063 toward/past dual_domain_supervised (predicted iter-3 hr ~0.37-0.41, extrapolating the iter1->iter2 +0.149/30-epoch slope sub-linearly as convergence approaches). FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr plateaus at or below 0.322 (or drops) at ep64, uswin has reached its training-convergence basin at uswin_c=24 -> it is CAPACITY-limited, not training-limited, and iter-4 must raise uswin_c (24->32) or add an lr-schedule rather than epochs (which cannot fit the wall much beyond 72 anyway). (5) HARD 20-min train+score budget; val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices (NOT reduced); grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP, bg_target=truth, metric=321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). (6) no control return.

advice_for_others: uswin-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=214, epochs=34, batch_size=4, lr=0.0005, uswin_c=32, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=900, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). ONE KNOB: CAPACITY uswin_c 24 -> 32 (every encoder level widens c, 2c, 4c, 8c; the WindowMSA at each level runs MHA on the wider dim with heads HELD at 4 -> head_dim = 32/4 = 8 valid, 24/4=6 before; uswin_c=32 is in the sanctioned TPE search space [16,24,32]; params ~3.95M -> ~6.9M, a (32/24)^2 = 1.778x conv+attention compute bump), with epochs TRADED DOWN 64 -> 34 to fit the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall. This is the same capacity-for-epochs trade the champion dual_domain_supervised just ran (c16->24, ep27->10). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) TRAJECTORY iter-1 ep10 c24 -> SSIM 0.885910 / hr 0.173021 in 328.96s; iter-2 ep40 c24 -> SSIM 0.914097 / hr 0.322063 in 737.72s; iter-3 ep64 c24 -> SSIM 0.924443 / hr 0.353196 in 1085.87s (CURRENT, #2 on the Mayo board). current config uswin_c=24 epochs=64. (2) LIMITER: the epochs lever is now BOTH wall-locked AND showing diminishing returns. WALL: iter-3 ep64 used 1085.87s = 90.5pct of the 1200s budget; the iter-3 note computed ep72 -> 1174s = 19.6 min (only 26s margin), so epochs cannot meaningfully rise. DIMINISHING RETURNS: hr gained +0.149 over ep10->40 (+30 ep) but only +0.031 over ep40->64 (+24 ep) -> the per-epoch hr slope is flattening, the c24 net is approaching its training-convergence basin. iter-3's OWN falsifier named this exact pivot: 'if hr plateaus ... iter-4 must raise uswin_c (24->32)'. The new lever is CAPACITY, not epochs. (3) ONE KNOB: uswin_c 24->32, epochs 64->34; ALL else held (train_n=200, val_n=214, bs=4, lr=5e-4, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). BUDGET-TRADE MATH (worst-case-sized, mirroring the champion's method): from the two measured c24 (epochs, elapsed_s) points (40,737.72),(64,1085.87): per_epoch_c24 = (1085.87-737.72)/(64-40) = 14.51 s/epoch; fixed_c24 (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure I/O) = 737.72 - 40*14.51 = 157.3s (predicts ep64 = 157.3 + 64*14.51 = 1086.0s vs actual 1085.87 -> calibration exact). A c24->c32 widening multiplies the U-Net+attention compute by (32/24)^2 = 1.778x; the per-sample 2304-view FBP adjoint is c-INDEPENDENT. WORST CASE (pessimistically assume EVERYTHING incl. the FBP adjoint scales 1.778x): per_epoch_worst = 14.51*1.778 = 25.80 s/epoch; fixed_worst = 157.3*1.778 = 279.7s. Largest epoch count fitting 1200s: (1200-279.7)/25.80 = 35.7 -> ep34 worst-case = 279.7 + 34*25.80 = 1156.9s = 19.3 min (43s margin inside the 1200s budget; sbatch wall is 30 min). ep36 worst-case = 1208.5s BUSTS the budget, so ep34 is the LARGEST epoch count guaranteed to fit even the worst case; epochs is sized to the worst-case bound, not the optimistic one (a wall-bust wastes the whole QOS slot). REALISTIC (FBP adjoint ~30pct of per-epoch, c-independent): per_epoch_real = 14.51*(0.30+0.70*1.778) = 22.42 s/epoch -> ep34 real ~ 243 + 34*22.42 = 1005s = 16.7 min, comfortable headroom. Train-only worst = 34*25.80 = 877s < max_train_s=900 backstop (set to 900 so train always halts leaving >=300s for the worst-case val+figure inside the 1200s budget; iter-3 used 1000 but the bigger net's fixed-cost grew, so 900 is the safe backstop). (4) HYPOTHESIS: 1.778x more representational capacity lifts hr above the iter-3 0.353196 toward/past the champion dual_domain_supervised's 0.365, even at the reduced ep34, because uswin's hr is flattening at c24 (training-basin) yet remains a strong Mayo image-domain denoiser and c32 is its top sanctioned capacity. Predicted iter-4 hr ~0.36-0.38. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.353196 at uswin_c=32/ep34, uswin has hit its representational ceiling on this val set (~0.355) AND/OR ep34 under-trained the bigger net more than the added capacity helped -> iter-5 either (a) keeps c32 and recovers epochs toward the wall if the measured c32 per-epoch is cheaper than the 25.80s worst case (i.e. ep34 left budget headroom), or (b) reverts to c24/ep64 and accepts 0.3532 as the uswin ceiling. (5) HARD 20-min train+score budget; val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices (NOT reduced); grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP, bg_target=truth, metric=321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). (6) no control return.

ARCHITECTURE NOTE: this solver trains ONLY a handful of nn.Parameter scalars (per-band log-scale x4, sigmoid slope+offset x2, per-outer soft-threshold + residual-blend) wrapped around a band-weighted aliasing-free FBP + a soft-thresholded dense-residual pass; with wu_n_outer=1 that is 4+2+1+1 = 8 trainable scalars (n_bands=4). All scalars are HARD-CLAMPED inside the solver (band_scale 0.1-3.0, blend -0.5-2.0, soft_thresh 1e-5-0.05) so the optimizer cannot run away. CONFIG: wu_n_outer=1 (the discarded boundary-slice run flagged n_outer=1 as mandatory -- behavior hint only; it also HALVES the costly 2x-dense-projector residual pass per sample, the dominant per-slice cost), wu_n_bands=4 (default), lr=1e-2 (solver default; aggressive lr is fine for ~8 scalars and converges fast), epochs=6 (8 clamped scalars settle in very few epochs at lr=1e-2 -- this is NOT a deep net that under-trains; the real risk here is the opposite structural FBP ceiling, not under-convergence), train_n=200 stratified across the 4 Wagner train patients ps-groups, val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices, batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED by per-sample-ps (each train step + each val slice swaps model.proj AND model.dense_proj to its slice ps), grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY Mayo guard: the 2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise), lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0 (defer to iter-2+; the discarded run hinted weight_decay tuning around its run-best iter-11, treat as loose behavior hint only), loss_base=mse, seed=42. BUDGET REASONING: the solver has NO in-code max_train_s wall hook (cannot add one -- must not edit the solver .py), so the budget is enforced by SIZING: with wu_n_outer=1 the per-sample cost is 1 band-weighted sparse-FBP (4-band backproject) + 1 forward_project + 1 dense-FBP + 1 back_project -- heavier than DD-UNet (iter-1 418s @ep8) but LIGHTER than the unrolled k=3 itnet_v3 (iter-1 738s @ep8) because there is no per-step unrolled DC loop; at only 6 epochs over 200 train slices the dominant cost is the 214-slice val pass at chunk=1 with the dense projector. This sizes train+score comfortably under the 20-min budget (30-min SLURM wall) with room for the figure. HYPOTHESIS: if I fit Wu-trainable at n_outer=1 / lr=1e-2 / ep=6 on 200 stratified Mayo train slices, I expect a finite val_ssim that lands in/near the LD-FBP baseline band (~0.84-0.89 SSIM, hr near 0), because Wu-trainable is a tuned-FBP family (band-reweighting + ONE soft-thresholded residual pass, NO image-domain CNN denoiser) and can only recover the small headroom that band weighting + a single residual correction buys over plain FBP -- it is structurally close to FBP, unlike the dual-domain U-Net families that landed hr~0.27. The discarded boundary-slice run hinted ~0.9135 SSIM at run-best iter-11 (loose behavior hint, NOT a validated number under the corrected 214-slice 321px-FOV metric). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric Wu-trainable baseline that iter-2+ will improve by tuning ONE knob (epochs/weight_decay first, then band/sigmoid knobs).

Wu-trainable is a band-reweighted aliasing-free FBP + soft-thresholded dense-residual pass(es) with NO image-domain CNN denoiser; epochs are inert and frequency-band count++ destabilises -- it sits hr~0.04-0.05 just above the LD-FBP floor and neither lever has moved it up. NEW PARAM COUNT: wu_n_bands+2+2*wu_n_outer = 4+2+2*2 = 10 trainable scalars (was 8 at iter-1; iter-3's 6-band/1-outer was also 10) -- the +2 over iter-1 are the per-outer log_soft_thresh + residual_blend for the new second pass.
